title: OneQuery: Unified Sequence-to-Structure Generation for Multilingual E-commerce Query Understanding
summary: Multilingual e-commerce search requires robust query understanding to convert cross-lingual user queries with varied linguistic patterns into standardized semantic representations that support retrieval and ranking. However, traditional Query Understanding systems suffer from error accumulation, separately optimized subtasks that ignore their mutual correlations, and high maintenance costs. To address these issues, this paper proposes OneQuery, a unified generative framework for multilingual query understanding based on domain-specific large language models in e-commerce. We reformulate four subtasks, namely Language Recognition, Spelling Correction, Translation, and Query Tagging, into a unified Sequenceto-Structure autoregressive generation process constrained by predefined schemas, and design a three-stage progressive training pipeline with multi-task reinforcement learning alignment. OneQuery demonstrates consistent gains over baselines across all tasks and remains effective across different backbone sizes, and online experiments in the AliExpress e-commerce search scenario further confirm its practical value for industrial deployment.
tldr: Multilingual e-commerce search requires robust query understanding to convert cross-lingual user queries with varied linguistic patterns into standardized semantic representations that support retrieval and ranking. However, traditional Query Understanding systems suffer from error accumulation, separately optimized subtasks that ignore their mutual correlations, and high maintenance costs.
deep_summary: Multilingual e-commerce search requires robust query understanding, but traditional pipelines suffer from error accumulation and high maintenance costs due to separately optimized subtasks. To solve this, the authors propose OneQuery, a unified generative framework that reformulates language recognition, spelling correction, translation, and query tagging into a single schema-guided sequence-to-structure generation task. The approach relies on a progressive three-stage training pipeline: joint single-task SFT, data synthesis via iterative field completion, and task-aware multi-objective reinforcement learning alignment using GRPO. Experiments on AliExpress data show consistent performance gains over traditional pipelines across 4B, 8B, and 14B model scales, outperforming few-shot proprietary LLMs. Online A/B tests further confirm practical business impact with improved conversion and relevance metrics.
key_ideas: Reformulate language recognition, spelling correction, translation, and query tagging into a unified sequence-to-structure JSON generation task using domain-specific large language models.
Implement an Iterative Field Completion data synthesis strategy to generate 3.6 million fully annotated training samples from partially annotated task-specific data.
Use a progressive three-stage training pipeline combining joint single-task SFT, hybrid dataset fine-tuning, and task-aware multi-objective RL alignment (GRPO) with rule-based rewards.
Design task-aware rule-based rewards (including exact match and edit distance similarity) with non-uniform weights to balance gradient contributions and mitigate multi-task optimization conflicts.
results: Evaluated on 19,087 multilingual search queries from AliExpress, the 14B model improved Language Recognition accuracy from 0.9514 to 0.9665, Translation ROUGE-2 from 78.20 to 80.50, Spelling Correction F1 from 0.8568 to 0.8717, and Query Tagging F1 from 0.8128 to 0.8366. Online A/B tests on AliExpress showed a 0.5% improvement in list-to-payment conversion rate (L2P) and a 0.8-point gain in relevance evaluation.
apply_at_iconic: Adopt the schema-guided sequence-to-structure generation paradigm to unify THE ICONIC's search query understanding pipeline (combining spelling correction, translation, intent, and entity tagging) to reduce error propagation and serving overhead.
Apply the iterative field completion and data synthesis strategy to bootstrap a unified query understanding or product attribute extraction model using partially annotated historical logs.

Deploy a hybrid serving architecture with large offline-cached models for head queries and a distilled lightweight student model for real-time tail queries to meet strict e-commerce search latency constraints.

title: Impact of AI-Powered Recommendation Systems on Consumer Purchase Intention in E-Commerce: A Review
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered recommendation systems have become a central feature of e-commerce platforms. By analysing browsing history, past purchases, search behaviour, ratings, and demographic information, these systems suggest products that appear relevant to individual consumers. This paper reviews existing literature on the relationship between AI-based recommendation systems and consumer purchase intention in e-commerce. The review finds that recommendation quality, personalization, perceived usefulness, trust, and reduced search effort generally strengthen purchase intention. However, privacy concerns, perceived intrusiveness, algorithmic bias, and lack of transparency can reduce consumer acceptance. The paper concludes that AI recommendations can improve consumer engagement and sales conversion, but e-commerce firms must balance personalization with data privacy, explainability, and ethical data use

The study examines how platforms analyze user browsing history, past purchases, search behavior, ratings, and demographics to suggest relevant products. By synthesizing previous research, the review identifies key factors that influence consumer behavior, including recommendation quality, personalization, trust, and perceived usefulness. It also highlights potential negative factors such as privacy concerns, intrusiveness, algorithmic bias, and a lack of transparency. Ultimately, the paper concludes that while AI recommendations boost engagement and conversion rates, retailers must carefully balance personalization with privacy and ethical considerations.

title: Interactive-Active-AI/NextTransformer
summary: :sunrise: A comprehensive, cutting-edge open-source framework for next-generation Transformers/LLM, with compute-matched benchmarking and a platform for autonomous architecture research.
tldr: sunrise: A comprehensive, cutting-edge open-source framework for next-generation Transformers/LLM, with compute-matched benchmarking and a platform for autonomous architecture research.
deep_summary: NextTransformer is an open-source framework, benchmark, and auto-research platform designed to evaluate next-generation Transformer architectures under strictly controlled computational budgets. The framework ensures fair comparisons by training diverse variants—including recurrent depth, sparse and linear attention, residual-stream choices, and hybrids—on identical data tokens and training FLOPs. It features Arena v2 for agent-native research, comprehensive leaderboards, and an extensive model zoo containing baseline, residual, looped, sparse, linear, and hybrid configurations. The main findings provide transparent, audited performance metrics across different architectures to guide efficient language model scaling and design.
key_ideas: Fair training protocol enforcing identical data, tokenizers, contexts, and training FLOPs per token to evaluate different transformer architectures objectively.
Comprehensive model zoo spanning baseline, residual, looped, sparse, linear, and hybrid architectures sharing a single trainer and data pipeline.
Arena v2 framework enabling agent-native autonomous research through a research gym with MCP tools and metered compute.
Mixture of Experts (MoE) track evaluating sparse models using MoE-CORE metrics across standardized sizes and token counts.
results: Models are evaluated across 49.152B input tokens using 46,875 updates, with MoE tracks comparing d768 at 14.07B tokens and d1024 at 34.06B tokens.
apply_at_iconic: Leverage alternative transformer architectures like linear attention or hybrid models from the model zoo to optimize latency and efficiency for e-commerce product recommendations or search ranking.
Adopt the strict compute-matching and evaluation protocol principles to fairly benchmark custom language models or recommendation algorithms against internal baselines.

title: eust-w/opengeniemaster
summary: Open-source embodied agent framework: execution, feedback, and continual improvement
tldr: Open-source embodied agent framework: execution, feedback, and continual improvement
deep_summary: OpenGenieMaster is an open-source embodied continuous harness designed for continuous multi-robot operations, replicating the GenieMaster framework without modifying policy weights. It utilizes an Embodied Execution Protocol (EEP) exposed as an MCP server to allow coding agents like Claude Code or Codex to call robot capabilities, provide multimodal guidance, read physical feedback, and resume interrupted tasks. The system incorporates shared admission safety interlocks, versioned long-term memory with reflection, and a semantic multi-robot simulator. According to the benchmark results, the system achieves a 93.2 percent overall success rate and maintains high generalization on novel items.
key_ideas: Implement EEP over MCP to expose robot capabilities, multimodal guidance, and task continuity directly to coding agents via standard stdio.
Maintain task continuity by binding work items to robots with dependencies and state persistence, enabling resumption from the next incomplete step after interruption.
Enforce safety through shared admission interlocks that reject requests if robots are stopped, calibration fails, dependencies are unmet, or humans enter the workspace.
Reflect execution records into versioned, diffable, and rollbackable long-term memory without altering underlying policy weights.
results: In the built-in semantic simulator across 6 tasks and 100 trials per method, OpenGenieMaster achieved an overall success rate of 93.2 percent compared to 12.5 percent for end-to-end VLA.

title: HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent
summary: Slate recommendation, which presents users with a ranked item list in a single display, is ubiquitous across mainstream online platforms. While recent generative recommendation methods have shown strong potential in modeling item sequences with semantic IDs, directly applying them to industrial-scale slate recommendation faces a fundamental disconnect: entangled SID spaces confound high-level list planning, fine-grained autoregressive decoding over long sequences limits semantic planning efficiency, and token-level objectives misalign with holistic slate quality. In this paper, we propose HiGR, an industrial-scale hierarchical generative framework for slate recommendation that bridges this disconnect through a co-designed pipeline. First, HiGR learns structured SIDs via a Prefix-Contrastive Residual Quantized VAE (PCRQ-VAE). By enforcing high-level prefixes to capture shared semantics, PCRQ-VAE creates a controllable discrete space that acts as a prerequisite for efficient planning. Leveraging this structured space, our Hierarchical Slate Decoder (HSD) shifts autoregressive modeling from entangled token-level decoding to coarse-grained preference embeddings. This design significan…
affiliations: Sun Yat-sen University, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China
tldr: Slate recommendation, which presents users with a ranked item list in a single display, is ubiquitous across mainstream online platforms.
deep_summary: Slate recommendation systems typically rely on multi-stage pipelines that process items in isolation, causing a disconnect between token-level generation and holistic slate quality. To solve this, the authors propose HiGR, an industrial-scale hierarchical generative framework for slate recommendation developed by Tencent. HiGR introduces a Prefix-Contrastive Residual Quantized VAE (PCRQ-VAE) to learn structured semantic IDs, a Hierarchical Slate Decoder (HSD) for coarse-to-fine generation that reduces latency, and an ORPO-based listwise preference alignment mechanism for triple-objective optimization. Offline experiments and online A/B tests demonstrate that HiGR outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by over 10% in recommendation quality while achieving a 5x inference speedup and significant online engagement gains.
key_ideas: Use Prefix-Contrastive RQ-VAE (PCRQ-VAE) with contrastive constraints on the first D-1 codebook layers to enforce semantic prefix alignment while reserving the final layer for fine-grained item discrimination.

Implement a Hierarchical Slate Decoder (HSD) that separates generation into a coarse-grained slate planner (predicting preference embeddings) and a lightweight shared item generator (decoding SID tokens).
Incorporate an intra-list diversity (ILD) regularization term into preference planning to explicitly penalize redundancy among planned items without post-hoc filtering.
Apply Odds Ratio Preference Optimization (ORPO) for reference-free listwise preference alignment, constructing negative slates targeting ranking fidelity, genuine interest, and diversity.
results: HiGR was evaluated on a 1-billion-sample industrial dataset from Tencent and the KuaiRec dataset, outperforming baselines by over 10% in offline recommendation quality with a 5x inference speedup. Online A/B tests on Tencent platforms showed a 1.22% increase in watch time and a 1.73% increase in video plays.
apply_at_iconic: Apply HSD coarse-to-fine generation to homepage tile personalisation and category page slate generation to jointly optimize list-level diversity and relevance instead of independent item scoring.
Adapt PCRQ-VAE semantic tokenisation to catalog product data, using prefix-level contrastive alignment to improve category-aware product embeddings for visual search and recommendations.
Use ORPO-based listwise preference alignment to fine-tune generative recommendation models on multi-objective implicit feedback like conversion rates, basket size, and fashion style diversity.

This study develops an integrated framework combining aspect-based sentiment analysis and text clustering to identify product attributes, determine aspect-level sentiment, group semantically related customer complaints, and translate the resulting complaint patterns into product-improvement recommendations. A publicly available e-commerce review corpus containing 27,846 retained reviews was processed through text cleaning, sentence segmentation, aspect extraction, aspect-level sentiment classification, semantic text embedding, and complaint clustering. title: From Prediction to Thinking: A Review of Reasoning in Industrial Recommender System
summary: Thinking has become an increasingly visible theme in recommendation research, but the termcovers mechanisms with different purposes, computational costs, and evidential support. To ourknowledge, this work presents the first systematic review dedicated specifically to thinking andreasoning mechanisms in industrial recommender systems. We trace its development in orig-inal research involving major technology platforms, from behavioral prediction and semanticgrounding to explicit chain-of-thought, recommendation-specific post-training, latent reason-ing, and amortized reasoning services. We organize the literature along three complementaryaxes: what grounds an intermediate state, how that state is represented and consumed, andhow its usefulness is learned or verified. Twenty-five core reports involving Microsoft Research,Huawei, Shopee, Kuaishou, Tencent, Alibaba/Taobao, Meta, JD.com, Netflix, and Xiaohongshuare analyzed alongside historical foundations, search applications, and industrial alternatives.The evidence indicates that reasoning supervision, inference-time reasoning, and productionsystem improvements must be evaluated separately. tldr: This paper provides a systematic review of thinking and reasoning mechanisms in industrial recommender systems across major technology platforms. It traces developments from behavioral prediction and semantic grounding to explicit chain-of-thought, latent reasoning, and amortized services. The study categorizes these techniques along three complementary axes to understand intermediate computational states.

title: Rich-Media Re-Ranker: A User Satisfaction-Driven LLM Re-ranking Framework for Rich-Media Search
summary: Re-ranking plays a crucial role in modern information search systems by refining the ranking of initial search results to better satisfy user information needs. However, existing methods show two notable limitations in improving user search satisfaction: inadequate modeling of multifaceted user intents and neglect of rich side information such as visual perception signals. To address these challenges, we propose the Rich-Media Re-Ranker framework, which aims to enhance user search satisfaction through multi-dimensional and fine-grained modeling. Our approach begins with a Query Planner that analyzes the sequence of query refinements within a session, decomposing the query into clear and complementary sub-queries to enable broader coverage of users' potential intents. Subsequently, moving beyond primary text content, we integrate richer side information of candidate results, including signals modeling visual content generated by the VLM-based evaluator. title: SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders
summary: While Transformers have achieved remarkable success in LLMs through superior scalability, their application in industrial-scale ranking models remains nascent, hindered by the challenges of high feature sparsity and low label density. In this paper, we propose SORT (Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer), a scalable model designed to bridge the gap between Transformers and industrial-scale ranking models. We address the high feature sparsity and low label density challenges through a series of optimizations, including request-centric sample organization, local attention, query pruning and generative pre-training. Furthermore, we introduce a suite of refinements to the tokenization, multi-head attention (MHA), and feed-forward network (FFN) modules, which collectively stabilize the training process and enlarge the model capacity. To maximize hardware efficiency, we optimize our training system to elevate the model FLOPs utilization (MFU) to 45%. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SORT outperforms strong baselines and exhibits excellent scalability across data size, model size and sequence length, while remaining flexible at integrating diverse features. title: Decoupled Temporal Encoding for Generative Recommendation
summary: Positional encoding is a fundamental component of Transformer-based generative recommendation models, where user histories are modeled as autoregressive item sequences. Most positional encoding methods are inherited from natural language processing and mainly represent discrete item order. However, recommendation sequences go beyond ordered lists, as timestamps and temporal effects also shape item relations. Our work is motivated by a real-world food delivery and instant retail recommendation system, where user behavior exhibits multi-level temporal regularities, including recency effects, meal-time peaks, weekday-weekend shifts, and promotion-driven traffic bursts. Existing methods partially address this issue through timestamp features, interval embeddings, decay functions, or attention biases, but they usually inject heterogeneous temporal signals through a unified representation or a single modeling pathway, making it difficult to distinguish broad temporal dynamics from local order cues. title: Artificial intelligence recommendation systems and consumer purchase intention: A systematic literature review and research agenda
summary: Artificial intelligence recommendation systems now shape how consumers discover and evaluate products online, yet research on their influence on purchase intention remains scattered across theories, contexts and methods. A Scopus search covering January 2015 to March 2026 returned 1,779 records, which were screened to 397 and then to a final sample of 112 peer reviewed journal articles. title: LEAPS: An LLM-Empowered Adaptive Plugin in Taobao AI Search
summary: The rapid rise of large language models has shifted user search behavior from discrete keywords to natural-language, multi-constraint queries—a shift existing e-commerce search architectures struggle to accommodate. Users face a dilemma: precise natural-language queries often trigger zero-result scenarios, while forced simplification yields noisy, generic results that overwhelm decision-making. To address this, we propose LEAPS (LLM-Empowered Adaptive Plugin in Taobao AI Search), which upgrades traditional search pipelines via a ''Broaden-and-Refine'' paradigm by attaching plugins at both ends. (1) Upstream, a Query Expander generates adaptive, complementary query combinations to maximize the candidate set, trained via a three-stage strategy of inverse data augmentation, posterior-knowledge supervised fine-tuning, and diversity-aware reinforcement learning. (2) Downstream, a Relevance Verifier filters noise by synthesizing multi-source signals (e.g., OCR text, reviews) with chain-of-thought reasoning. title: The Recall Ceiling of LLM Recommendation Reranking
summary: Some LLM-based recommendation rerankers are evaluated under an oracle protocol that guarantees the ground-truth item is present in the scored set, either by injecting it into the candidate list or by scoring it against sampled negatives. We show that this protocol overestimates realistic performance by 92-95% in NDCG@10 across three primary Amazon datasets, so oracle results do not transfer to deployment. The root cause is a recall ceiling: realistic retrieval covers only 2-19% of relevant items at K=100 across eight datasets in three domains (Amazon products, MovieLens movies, MIND news), placing a deterministic upper bound on any closed-candidate reranker's top-k NDCG (Theorem 1, E[NDCG@k] <= Recall@|W_pi| under LOO evaluation, where W_pi is the reranker's own candidate window). affiliations: University of Southern California,Viterbi School of Engineering, Los Angeles, CA, USA
tldr: Some LLM-based recommendation rerankers are evaluated under an oracle protocol that guarantees the ground-truth item is present in the scored set, either by injecting it into the candidate list or by scoring it against sampled negatives. title: Demand forecasting using machine learning.
summary: This diploma thesis compares different methods for daily retail sales forecasting, including statistical methods, machine learning algorithms, and deep learning models. Retail sales forecasting is crucial for supporting decisions related to inventory management, product availability and short term planning. However, fluctuations in demand and recurring temporal patterns make accurate sales forecasting a challenging task. The dataset used comprises 913,000 daily sales observations across 50 products and 10 stores, covering the period from January 2013 to December 2017. Prior to applying the forecasting methods, the data were analyzed for trend and seasonality, and features were engineered based on both the calendar and historical sales data. The statistical methods examined include Naive, Seasonal Naive, Moving Average, Holt Winters, and ARIMA/SARIMA. The machine learning models include Linear Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Feed Forward Neural Networks, LSTM, CNN and a hybrid CNN LSTM are also evaluated. The models are evaluated using forecasting error metrics, such as MAE, MSE, RMSE, MAPE and SMAPE. This study examines two forecasting scenarios: …

title: Recommender Systems Optimisation
AI-DRIVEN QUERY EXPANSION TECHNIQUES FOR ENHANCED SEARCH ENGINE PERFORMANCE
summary: With the rapid growth of digital data, searching and information retrieval is becoming increasingly complex. Traditional keyword-based search techniques can struggle with short, vague, and context-specific questions, providing limited or irrelevant answers. In this study, we propose an AI-driven paradigm for query expansion combining transformer-based contextual embedding and relevance-sensitive ranking to boost the effectiveness of search tasks. The proposed approach uses the idea of semantically related expansion phrases based on the contextual similarity and integrates them with the conventional TF-IDF or BM25 to attain equitable retrieval. The final step of end-of-user evaluation determines whether the attained outcomes are relevant to the applications of the user. The study also considers how the technology of AI-based query optimization is being utilized in eCommerce, finance, and flight data analysis systems. Such application proves that the usage of artificial intelligence, deep learning, and natural language processing enables the transformation of the information retrieval from the pure data-based technique into a more semantic one.

title: RoFiGR: Coarse Routing, Fine Refinement via Level-Adaptive Distillation in Multimodal Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommenders predict an item's semantic identifier (SID) one code at a time. Early codes select broad branches, so a routing error can exclude relevant items before fine-grained prediction begins. In multimodal recommendation, these coarse decisions must reflect collaborative preferences as well as item semantics. We introduce RoFiGR, a two-tree recommender that uses collaborative information in both SID construction and generation. It aligns cumulative L1-L2 code vectors with frozen collaborative item embeddings and explicitly encodes item distance and source level in the serialized history. During generation, a sequential teacher supervises legal branches. Fixed coarse-level weights maintain routing supervision, while a bounded adaptive residual allocates additional weight according to teacher-student demand. On Instruments, Arts, and Games, RoFiGR improves all five ranking metrics over the evaluated external baselines. Five-seed paired tests with Holm correction support the main NDCG@10 improvements. title: Temporal Moment Generation: A New Recommendation Task and Cost-Efficient Distillation for Outbound Marketing at Scale
summary: Outbound marketing at scale relies on content-first programs and item-ranking pipelines that match a fixed catalog to recent activity, missing the long-horizon interests and seasonal context (e.g., back-to-school, Earth Day) that make a message relevant. Missing these signals has played a key role in engagement declines of up to 18% year-over-year, with 55% of push notifications rated irrelevant by users. We make two contributions. First, we formalize temporal moment generation as a new recommendation task, distinct from item ranking: rather than scoring a catalog against a customer, the system starts from why a specific customer should be reached now. Given a customer behavioral signal profile and reference time T, it generates temporally-grounded moments---each a name, trigger, bounded activation window, and message hook, plus tiered search phrases for product retrieval---feeding a downstream retrieval and messaging pipeline. title: Challenges and Methods of Causal Promotions Recommendation in E-commerce
summary: This article tackles the challenges of causal promotions recommendation in e-commerce, with a focus on scalable, real-world implementations for managing large-scale promotional campaigns. We begin by outlining the unique domain-specific complexities of promotions in dynamic settings such as online travel platforms, including triggered costs, sparse conversions, and multi-product interactions. To address these, we introduce a steering framework that enables systematic, continuous experimentation and measurement. We then present methods and best practices for causal uplift modeling and constrained optimization, highlighting a retrospective estimation approach that leverages transaction-only data. These contributions are validated through real-world deployments at Booking.com, demonstrating how causal machine learning can be operationalized to optimize promotions effectively. Our work bridges rigorous methodology with practical business needs, offering a blueprint for balancing strategic impact and operational constraints in industrial settings.

summary: Demand forecasting and market trend analytics together constitute the analytical foundation of contemporary strategic and operational decision making. title: E-GenRM: Generative Reward Modeling for Open-Ended E-Commerce Shopping Agents
summary: We present E-GenRM (E-commerce Generative Reward Model), a generative reward model tailored to e-commerce shopping agents. User expectations are shifting from simple product queries to open-ended shopping tasks. However, existing trajectories and reward designs remain largely bounded by current agent usage patterns and known failures, providing limited guidance for further capability improvement. These limitations call for an integrated reward modeling framework for open-ended shopping agent tasks. On the data side, E-GenRM leverages naturally occurring user behavior across the shopping app to construct diverse, long-horizon conversational trajectories beyond established usage patterns. On the modeling side, E-GenRM first learns from behavior-grounded evaluation chains through supervised fine-tuning. It is then optimized through criterion-guided reinforcement learning, which rewards correct preference judgments and evidence-supported factual claims under each criterion. Personalized hard-negative training further improves its sensitivity to user preferences reflected in shopping behavior, beyond explicit requirements. title: Evolving Creatives with Clicks: CTR-Driven Advertising image Editing via Attribute Disentanglement and Preference Alignment
summary: The optimization objective for e-commerce advertising creatives has shifted from aesthetic quality to online business metrics like click-through rate (CTR). Recent methods generate appealing ad images from product images by constructing CTR-based reward signals and refining prompt generation via Reinforcement Learning. Such paradigms equally penalize all attributes within an underperforming image, even though some are actually beneficial to clicks. In this work, we propose Evolving Creatives with Clicks (ECC), which reformulates creative optimization as fine-grained editing rather than generation from scratch. ECC selectively refines attributes that hurt CTR while preserving those that contribute positively. Specifically, faced with a rich attribute space across massive images, ECC first identifies 28 attributes significantly correlated with CTR via ANOVA and Random Forest regression. Based on attribute contrasts between images with disparate CTRs, we instruction-tune a prompt model to generate editing suggestions, then refine it with real click preferences since reference-derived suggestions are not uniformly beneficial. title: SepLRM: A Foundation Model Paradigm for Recommendation
summary: Large recommendation models (LRMs) improve recommendation performance by scaling behavior sequence length, model capacity, and training compute. However, the return on investment (ROI) of continued scaling deteriorates as marginal gains diminish and long-sequence encoding costs rise, especially when this computation is repeatedly executed by distinct models for diverse recommendation stages and business scenarios. To address this issue, we propose SepLRM, a recommendation foundation model (RFM) paradigm that identifies reusable sequence encoding and reorganizes multiple end-to-end (E2E) LRMs into one RFM and multiple independently optimized vertical models (VMs). The RFM adopts an encoder-decoder architecture and exports its final-layer encoder state as the shared key-value (KV) cache that is independent of downstream task-offered candidates. Unlike candidate-specific logits or aggregated user embeddings, the KV cache preserves fine-grained behavioral information. Separation at this native KV interface also allows each VM to construct candidate-conditioned queries while retaining the same query-KV interaction as its E2E counterpart, enabling high-fidelity capability transfer. title: ZeroGR: Filtering-First Constrained Decoding for Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommendation is gaining traction in production, retrieving items by generating their identifiers one token at a time. The generated sequences must identify relevant catalog items, so constrained decoding couples relevance scoring with validity filtering. Because most possible sequences are invalid, scoring before filtering wastes computation on candidates that will be discarded. Our evaluation shows that filtering first can avoid this work with negligible impact on recommendation quality. We present ZeroGR, a filtering-first constrained decoding system for generative recommendation. ZeroGR uses a step-sliced filtering index to reduce GPU memory use by tailoring data representations to each decoding step. Its execution engine adopts shared-slot execution to accelerate data exchange across stages and hybrid projection to adapt computation to workload patterns, thereby reducing execution overhead. During index refreshes, ZeroGR applies layout-guided streaming construction to speed up updates and limit serving interference. title: Explainable AI-Driven Recommendation Systems and Consumer Buying Behaviour: The Mediating Role of Trust and Perceived Personalization in E-Commerce
summary: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) in e-commerce has transformed consumer interactions with digital platforms through algorithmic recommendation systems. title: Toward User-Centered Agentic Recommendation: When Does Platform Competition Benefit Users?
summary: Conventional recommender systems operate within platform-specific catalogs, limiting access to potentially valuable resources across platforms. We propose user-centered agentic recommendation, a paradigm in which user agents compare recommendations from competing platform agents, and formalize their interaction as a repeated game. Platforms strategically modify descriptions without changing intrinsic item value, while each user agent assesses platform credibility using feedback from consumed items only. Our analysis shows that expanded resource access need not improve user welfare: strategic misrepresentation and limited verification can offset the benefits of platform competition. We quantify when platform credibility assessment allows users to benefit from broader access despite strategic exaggeration. Our analysis identifies resource and reporting conditions that guarantee higher average welfare than the original platform with an interaction budget linear in platform count. Experiments on synthetic and Amazon-grounded markets show that credibility assessment can improve finite-horizon utility, while its benefits depend on market size and mechanism parameters.

title: CITE: Contextual Item Transition Embeddings for Generative Recommendation with Parallel Semantic Identifiers
summary: Recommendation systems are widely used to help users discover relevant products, media, and services from large catalogs. Generative recommendation has emerged as a promising direction because it formulates next-item prediction as a generation task and supports structured representations for large catalogs. In particular, parallel semantic identifiers predict all identifier positions simultaneously, making it possible to use long semantic identifiers. However, scoring candidates solely through parallel semantic code probabilities models item transitions indirectly and lacks an explicit term for the directed relation between the latest item and each candidate. To address this limitation, we propose Contextual Item Transition Embeddings (CITE). CITE introduces an item-level transition score conditioned on the encoded history and the latest item, with separate source and destination embeddings to model the two roles of a directed transition. It keeps the parallel semantic identifier generator fixed and adds the transition score to the original semantic score using a coefficient selected on validation data. title: Graph-Based Discovery of Product Exposure Neighborhoods in E-Commerce Search
summary: Product discovery in e-commerce is increasingly mediated by search engines, where products repeatedly compete for user attention across thousands of search queries. title: Recommender Systems: Model Governance
A hybrid AI framework for hyper-personalized recommendations and customer engagement prediction in e-commerce
summary: The explosion of e-commerce has led to an increase in the demand for smart systems that can provide hyper-personalized experiences and enhance customer engagement. title: Embedding Surgery: Localized Updates for Adaptive Ranking Correction in Dense Retrieval
summary: Dense retrieval systems are core components of modern search engines, recommendation platforms, and retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. They encode documents and queries into dense embeddings, enabling efficient semantic search via vector similarity. However, because document embeddings are computed offline and stored in static indexes, these systems struggle to adapt to user feedback or evolving search intent. title: AGR: Agentic Generative Retrieval with Tool-Augmented Search
summary: Large-scale search and recommendation systems derive much of their retrieval quality from rich, heterogeneous features, yet existing generative retrieval (GR) methods struggle to exploit such feature ecosystems efficiently. Static feature injection either encodes all available signals or places them according to predetermined schemes, increasing serving cost and introducing irrelevant or conflicting evidence. More fundamentally, existing methods cannot adaptively determine when a feature is needed, which feature to select, or where it should influence hierarchical Semantic ID (SID) generation. We propose Agentic Generative Retrieval (AGR), a tool-augmented paradigm that interleaves SID generation with on-demand feature acquisition. Conditioned on the request and decoded SID prefix, AGR decides whether to invoke a tool, which feature to acquire, and where its observation should influence subsequent decoding, thereby steering generation toward feature-consistent SID branches. title: African Journal of Recommender Systems
Theoretically Sound Item Similarity Measures for Recommender Systems
summary: Quantifying the similarity between items is fundamental to neighborhood-based collaborative filtering, yet many commonly used similarity measures are heuristics that lack theoretical justification. The use of heuristics forces practitioners to rely on empirical trial-and-error, offering little insight into why certain measures outperform others or how they might be improved. In this paper, we present a principled approach for designing item similarity measures grounded in probabilistic modeling and parameter estimation. By adopting this formal perspective, we derive two previously overlooked similarity measures based on the Bernoulli and multinomial distributions. Through an extensive ablation study we highlight the critical role of bias, probabilistic smoothing, treating the unknowns correctly, and choosing appropriate probability distributions. Finally, we show that the commonly used cosine similarity can be interpreted as the solution to a specific optimization problem, thereby providing a novel perspective on this decades-old heuristic.

title: HASTE: Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommendation models have shown promising results by representing items as semantic IDs and generating these IDs autoregressively. We address these challenges with HASTE (Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for generaTive rEcommendation), a unified training framework that introduces hierarchical and attribute-specific supervision. title: Dynamic Click Destinations: Personalizing Post Ad-Click Landing Experiences

DCD applies to any post-click destination decision where the system can choose among destination options at click time and downstream conversion feedback is available. title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used throughout e-commerce workflows to generate content that informs purchasing decisions and supports customer interactions. Evaluating these systems requires accounting for user needs, product evidence, structural constraints, and business requirements that are not fully captured by general-purpose writing benchmarks. title: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks for Daily Apparel Retail Demand Forecasting: A Comparative Evaluation Across Forecasting Models
summary: Operational apparel forecasting requires comparisons that combine strong classical baselines, modern learning architectures, sensitivity analysis, and evaluation across multiple forecast origins. This study benchmarks nine methods for one-step-ahead daily forecasting using 1403 observations of a retailer-defined potential-sales measure from 11 apparel categories in Türkiye. title: RITE: Evaluating End-to-End Resilience to Silent Tool Errors in E-Commerce Agentic Systems
summary: Tool-using LLM agents increasingly answer e-commerce queries through multi-step tool interactions. The expected output of a tool call can shift between agent development and execution, allowing a plausible but incorrect value to be returned without an explicit failure signal. These silent errors may propagate through subsequent decisions into final answers. To study agents' resilience across this end-to-end process, we formulate Silent-error Resilience Task, an interactive task that evaluates whether they complete the original query after a silent error corrupts an intermediate state. We introduce RITE, a benchmark built from human-authored industrial workflows and production-log-derived inputs. To enable controlled and reproducible evaluation, we use a semantic error taxonomy to inject errors into fixed workflow prefixes, freeze recorded tool behavior, and let agents continue freely. It contains 167 matched units across nine e-commerce workflows, yielding 501 silent-error, correct-value, and explicit-failure instances. title: Recommender System as Slow and Fast Thinkers
summary: Sequential recommendation models are foundational to modern personalized services, yet their effectiveness varies substantially across heterogeneous user environments. In particular, static one-pass recommenders often perform well on common behavior patterns but degrade on operationally challenging user groups, such as users with longer histories or less mainstream item profiles. To address this limitation, we propose \textsc{DS-Frame}, an adaptive fast--slow inference framework for sequential recommendation. \textsc{DS-Frame} combines a Fast System for efficient routine prediction, a Slow System for iterative latent refinement, and a learned selector that routes each sample under a controllable computation budget. Experiments on five real-world datasets show that \textsc{DS-Frame} consistently improves representative sequential recommendation backbones, with larger gains on challenging groups and effective accuracy--efficiency trade-offs. This highlights the potential of adaptive inference for more efficient and robust recommendation. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/ZichenYuan233/Recommender-System-as-Slow-and-Fast-Thinkers}{this link}.

title: Conformal Prediction for Statistically Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge in Recommender Systems
summary: LLM-as-a-judge has emerged as a promising strategy for evaluating recommender systems. Yet, treating simulated ratings as real feedback can make unreliable evaluation appear reliable. This risk is especially consequential in sensitive domains such as nutrition and health. In this paper, we treat the LLM-as-a-judge paradigm as a calibrated relevance simulation problem: an LLM-based simulator predicts human preferences from user and item representations, and conformal prediction converts them into uncertainty intervals. To account for the nature of recommendation, we introduce stratified conformal calibration by user rating variance. Experiments under three LLMs and seven conformal prediction methods show that point estimates of preferences hide failures on low-rating items, while conformal interval width is driven by user-level heterogeneity. title: Platform Recommendation and Competition in Search Markets
summary: Recommendation rules affect both sellers' incentives and the alternatives consumers expect to find. We develop a framework for evaluating these rules with heterogeneous sellers, endogenous pricing and advertising, and costly consumer search. For a broad class of separable recommendation scores, we establish conditions under which a unique market equilibrium exists. Three applications illustrate the use of the framework. A stronger reward for low prices does not necessarily lower equilibrium prices and benefit consumers when products are sufficiently differentiated in qualities. Quality guidance can lower the price of each product and benefit consumers while raising the average transaction price. With heterogeneous match distributions, a reward for the best initial inspection can help consumers with advertising fixed and harm them when advertising adjusts. A two-type design extension shows that no finite optimum over implementable outcomes uses positive weights on both quality and low prices, even when the platform values consumer surplus.

title: SPRIG: Semantic-ID-enhanced Paths for Knowledge Graph-based Generative Recommendation
summary: Recommender systems leveraging generative models often generate item identifiers directly, rather than ranking catalog items by a recommendation score. These two lines have complementary limitations: SID-based models lack relational grounding, while KG-based generative recommenders still represent items as arbitrary, opaque tokens tied to large embedding tables, limiting parameter sharing and generalization. title: A systematic benchmarking pipeline for demand forecasting and inventory-aware supply chain decision support
summary: Demand forecasting has been shown to be one of the key facilitators of successful supply chain and inventory management. In this work, we introduce a benchmarking pipeline for demand forecasting in retail that includes data preprocessing, comparative benchmarking of different machine learning/deep learning (ML/DL) approaches, and decision-focused evaluation. Several standard forecasting models, such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), CNN-LSTM, and XGBoost, are compared using a unified experimental pipeline on benchmark retail datasets. summary: Cognitive factors are associated with online purchase intentions in developing economies, and the linear models conventionally used to study them can miss non-linear patterns. title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction
summary: LLM-based recommendation agents can search catalogs, inspect products, ask users, and revise rejected recommendations. However, these behaviors are often governed by hand-designed workflows, while existing training methods optimize isolated components such as query rewriting or list ranking rather than the interaction policy as a whole. title: ReSID: Rethinking Long-Tail Retrieval in Generative Recommendation through Item Reachability
summary: Generative recommendation (GR) represents items with discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) and casts retrieval as sequence generation. Under skewed interaction distributions and tight serving budgets, GR struggles to retrieve long-tail items. In this work, we are the first to study long-tail reachability across the complete pipeline of SID construction, decoding, and matching. We find that under equal code lengths, parallel SID construction consistently outperforms sequential SIDs on tail items. Moreover, even when full generation fails, decoded sequences carry locally consistent information that retrieves relevant tail items via partial matching. Yet this recovery is bounded by upstream search, failing once beam search prunes all prefixes completable within a fixed mismatch tolerance. Motivated by these findings, we propose ReSID to jointly preserve and recover tail candidates. Built on long parallel SIDs, ReSID pairs popularity-debiased and user-semantic-aware beam search to keep promising paths alive with partial SID matching to recover items from surviving tokens. title: Think-to-Personalize: Unifying Reasoning and Retrieval for User-Centric Personalized Dense Retrieval
summary: Dense retrieval has become a cornerstone of modern local-lifestyle e-commerce search by encoding queries and items into semantic embedding spaces. title: Learning from Unreachable Rewards: Hint-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Generative Recommendation
summary: Semantic-ID generative recommenders represent each item as a short sequence of discrete semantic tokens and predict the next item by autoregressively generating this token sequence. title: Improving Ads Ranking Models with Auxiliary Supervision: Techniques and Insights
summary: Accurate prediction of post-click Conversion Rate (CVR) is essential for personalized ad delivery in the advertising industry. Traditional ads ranking models rely on conversion events (e.g., a user purchasing an item) as ground truth labels for training. However, these conversion events are often sparse or missing, which limits the effectiveness of model learning. The primary contributions of this paper are: (1) a case study on the use of auxiliary supervision from a diverse set of user events and metadata signals beyond traditional conversion events, and (2) advanced modeling techniques designed to maximize the value of these signals. We detail architectural innovations such as linearized labels for improved auxiliary signal precision, a split architecture to facilitate training task decomposition, and a novel Label Combination (LaCo) approach for robustly managing noisy auxiliary data. Empirical results demonstrate that these methods deliver measurable improvements in ranking models, underscoring their versatility and effectiveness across recommendation systems and related domains.

title: Generative Recommenders Forget the Long Tail: Restoring Memorization in Retrieval and Ranking
summary: Generative recommenders replace the retrieve-then-rank cascade with a single model: beam search over semantic item identifiers performs retrieval, and the same likelihood performs ranking. We show that this shared score makes them forget long-tail items twice. In retrieval, beam search keeps identifier prefixes by the probability mass of their subtrees, so tail items are pruned early, and a wider beam admits few more of them. In ranking, the likelihood places tail items below head items even when they are admitted, so expanding retrieval alone brings little or no gain. Both failures reflect missing item-level memorization (i.e., direct recall of which items co-occur), which collaborative filtering provides and shared-prefix generation lacks. To this end, we propose CAPE (Co-occurrence-Aware Pool Expansion), a training-free plug-in that restores memorization at both stages: (i) a memorization channel retrieves co-occurrence-supported tail items outside the beam and scores them with the frozen generator, and (ii) memorization-calibrated ranking fuses the generator likelihood with co-occurrence evidence while keeping the generator's first item. title: LLM-Based Feature Extraction for Multi-Criteria Inventory Classification
summary: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. title: KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation
summary: Coordinating multiple recommendation objectives (e.g., click and conversion) is critical for real-world generative recommendation (GR). However, since a positive item in GR can be retrieved only when its tokens are successively selected at every decoding step, traditional item-wise methods lack fine-grained token-wise supervision to guide intermediate steps. Motivated by its success in foundation models, we consider introducing multi-objective on-policy distillation (MOPD) into GR to distill two single-objective teachers into a student at each token. Yet, we find that in vanilla MOPD, (i) teachers exhibit unequal distillation difficulty at each token (i.e., token-level imbalance), and (ii) the harder-to-distill teacher varies across tokens (i.e., cross-token inconsistency), leaving each objective poorly learned at certain steps and hindering positive item retrieval for both objectives, leading to suboptimal performance. title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
summary: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior digital actions remain valid. Whether current agents can reliably handle these changes remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce EgoUseBench, a benchmark for evaluating Ego Use across three interaction settings with different levels of first-person context. tldr: The paper introduces EgoUseBench to benchmark computer-use agents under evolving first-person contexts from AI wearables and smart glasses. It explores how agents can identify objects and activities from first-person observations and ground digital tasks in surrounding physical environments. The framework highlights the challenges agents face when dealing with incomplete or ambiguous first-person viewpoints.

title: ChoirRec: Semantic User Grouping via LLMs for Conversion Rate Prediction of Low-Activity Users
summary: Accurately predicting conversion rates (CVR) for low-activity users remains a fundamental challenge in large-scale e-commerce recommender systems. For these users, existing approaches face three critical limitations: (i) data dominated by high-activity users may introduce noisy and mismatched signals for learning low-activity users' preferences; (ii) insufficient interaction information; and (iii) a systemic training bias toward high-activity users. title: Graph-GRPO: Dependency-Aware Credit Assignment for Generative E-commerce Search Relevance
summary: Search relevance modeling is a core task in e-commerce search systems, assessing how well a user query matches candidate products. Rather than relying on a single holistic matching signal, relevance judgment often requires structured reasoning over query understanding, product understanding, and facet-level matching. With large language models (LLMs), this process is increasingly formulated as chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and optimized with reinforcement learning (RL). However, existing RL methods mainly rely on outcome-level rewards and treat the entire reasoning chain as a single optimization unit. This makes it difficult to distinguish faulty reasoning steps from correct intermediate ones, leading to misaligned credit assignment. Although process-reward methods provide denser supervision, they often treat reasoning steps independently and ignore dependency-driven error propagation, making responsibility attribution difficult and limiting the optimization of structured relevance reasoning. title: Semantic Search At LinkedIn
summary: Semantic search with large language models (LLMs) enables retrieval by meaning rather than keyword overlap, but scaling it requires major inference efficiency advances. We present LinkedIn's LLM-based semantic search framework for AI Job Search and AI People Search, combining an LLM relevance judge, embedding-based retrieval, and a compact Small Language Model trained via multi-teacher distillation to jointly optimize relevance and engagement. A prefill-oriented inference architecture co-designed with model pruning, context compression, and text–embedding hybrid interactions boosts ranking throughput by over 75× under fixed latency constraint while preserving near–teacher-level NDCG, enabling one of the first production LLM-based ranking systems with efficiency comparable to traditional approaches and delivering significant gains in quality and user engagement.

title: EchoTrace: Diagnosing Recursive Risks in LLM-Powered Recommender Systems
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into recommender systems as data augmenters, profile generators, and recommendation modules. While these roles can enhance semantic understanding and recommendation quality, they also introduce LLM-specific risks such as bias and hallucination. These risks become more critical in feedback-loop settings, where LLM-generated signals and recommendations recursively shape future training data and recommendation dynamics. In this paper, we propose a role-aware, phase-wise diagnostic framework for analyzing how LLM-induced risks emerge, propagate, and accumulate in LLM-powered recommender systems. Our framework combines controlled feedback-loop simulation with longitudinal phase-wise diagnosis across LLM-generated content, recommendation outputs, feedback-loop dynamics, and ecosystem-level effects. Experiments on widely used benchmarks show that LLM-based components can amplify popularity bias, introduce spurious signals through hallucination, and gradually produce polarized and self-reinforcing exposure patterns over time. The code for EchoTrace is available at https://github.com/DongUk-Park/EchoTrace.

title: MOSS: A Production Framework for Monitoring and Diagnosing Semantic Failures in Search and Recommendation Systems
summary: Detecting semantic failures in production recommendation and search systems is hard: behavioral metrics lag by days, manual review does not scale, and most LLM evaluation frameworks are designed for offline, fixed datasets rather than continuous operational monitoring. We present Model Sanity Service (MOSS), a production framework that addresses this operational gap by embedding LLM-based relevance scoring into a recurring monitoring loop with targeted sampling, strategy-aware prompting, structured alerting, and diagnostic follow-up prompting that categorizes failures into actionable root causes. MOSS has been running in production at a large U.S. retailer for over six months across recommendation, search, and offer surfaces, and has surfaced two confirmed serving defects. For one of these, a backfill blending defect, MOSS quantified the impact of the proposed fix offline as a 76.4\% relative reduction in alert rate. title: Characterizing Adversarial GEO via Implicit Brand Injection
summary: Generative search engines increasingly shape how users discover products, services, and commercial entities by generating answers from retrieved web content. This creates an opportunity to influence which brands appear in these answers by modifying the content available to the retrieval system. In this work, we study an adversarial generative engine optimization (GEO) setting in which a predefined brand is added to an article through a single contextually integrated mention. The challenge is to make the mention fit the surrounding article without making the content overtly promotional, while keeping it relevant enough to be retrieved and to influence the generated answer. To study this, we introduce Implicit Brand Injection (IBI), a multi-agent framework that identifies insertion locations, rewrites the selected sentence, verifies the edit, and selects the final candidate. To evaluate IBI at scale, we construct IBIBench, which contains 1,000 web articles and 60 synthetic brands across 12 diverse domains, with both endemic and non-endemic brand placements. title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
summary: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items. However, randomly initialized SID token embeddings and GR models trained from scratch do not directly inherit the semantic relations inherent in items, while inter-item collaborative relations are learned largely implicitly through token-level attention and next-token supervision. To address this limitation, we propose REGER, a unified framework that explicitly incorporates inter-item relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation. We pretrain the GR model through generative semantic retrieval, enabling it to inherit inter-item semantic similarity by learning to generate semantic neighbors' SIDs. We combine global attention with local attention aligned with SID boundaries to capture historical context and directed transitions between adjacent items. title: Multimodal attention fusion-based sequential recommendation system
summary: Sequential recommendation (SR) systems, which model dynamic user preferences from past behaviors, play a crucial role in e-commerce platforms. Recent studies on these systems have considered various types of information such as images and texts. However, multimodal data have not yet been fully exploited in SR settings. In this study, we propose an attention-based SR method that employs multimodal data for items such as images, texts, and categories. Specifically, we introduce a Multimodal Fusion Module that performs independent attention over item ID sequences and multimodal representations, and combines them through a Multimodal Fusion Function. In addition, modality-specific reconstruction losses for images, texts, and categories are incorporated as a multitask learning objective, serving as an implicit regularizer that improves generalization across diverse product domains. Experiments on four Amazon datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best overall results on three of the four datasets, yielding improvements of up to 2.5% in Recall@20 and 1.4% in NDCG@10 over the strongest baseline.

title: Penerapan Machine Learning untuk Fitur Rekomendasi Terpersonalisasi pada Platform E-Commerce Fashion Wanita
summary: Pertumbuhan e-commerce fashion wanita menunjukkan peluang besar namun juga tantangan dalam menghadirkan pengalaman belanja yang personal dan relevan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan Agile Scrum, dengan metode iteratif untuk pengembangan fitur rekomendasi yang dikembangkan dan dievaluasi menggunakan empat algoritma yaitu Logistic Regression, Random Forest, KNN, dan SVM. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi praktis terhadap peningkatan personalisasi dalam platform e-commerce serta pendekatan teknis yang dapat direplikasi pada konteks sistem serupa.

title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
summary: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. title: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Neural Network based Framework for Inventory Demand Forecasting
summary: Accurate inventory demand forecasting is essential for balancing service levels against operating costs in modern supply chains. Traditional statistical models often fail to capture non-linear demand patterns arising from seasonality, promotions and external disruptions. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that combines a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for automatic feature extraction with XGBoost regression for demand prediction. The framework integrates data preprocessing, normalization, feature engineering and model evaluation into a single predictive pipeline: the raw sales data are cleaned and normalized, the CNN extracts non-linear temporal and contextual features, and XGBoost uses these features to generate demand forecasts. The framework is evaluated on a publicly available retail sales dataset and compared with Linear Regression, ARIMA, Random Forest, XGBoost, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. title: Behavioral segmentation in e-commerce: A systematic literature review of data-driven meth-ods, applications, and research directions
summary: The topic of behavioral segmentation has emerged as an important research area in e-commerce since online stores increasingly depend on customer data for personalized, recommendation, retention, pricing, and marketing decisions. Behavioral segmentation is focused on observable actions such as browsing, clicking, buying, cart interaction, channel use, response to discounts, churn, and engagement. The existing studies are split across different methods, data sets, behavioral variables, and application areas making it difficult to understand the role that behavioral segmentation plays in e-commerce. The reviewed papers presented below are a systematic review of 44 studies in e-commerce behavioral segmentation published between 2016 and 2026. The selected papers were analyzed according to the selection process, inspired by the PRISMA framework. title: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model
summary: Whole image embeddings can under represent small objects and local attributes that distinguish relevant images for localized queries. We present LoCaR, a training free framework for localized text to image retrieval with frozen vision language models. LoCaR constructs and utilizes independent proposals (SAM2) focusing on the object so as to get a more localized representation that independently encodes each region using the frozen visual encoder. We further study paired-support adaptation as an optional residual that uses matched text region exemplars without updating the underlying encoders. We also introduce LOCFG, a Visual Genome derived benchmark designed to evaluate localized retrieval for smaller and more challenging referents. Across several vision language backbones, our results show that improving the region representation itself is the main source of gain.
tldr: The paper presents LoCaR, a training-free framework for localized text-to-image retrieval using frozen vision-language models to address the limitations of whole-image embeddings. It uses SAM2 to construct independent object proposals, generating localized representations that independently encode each region. Results introduce a new Visual Genome derived benchmark, LOCFG, for evaluating localized retrieval.

title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Finite-Beam Reachability and Continuous-Query Generation in Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommendation (GR) of social media platforms commonly retrieves items by autoregressively decoding discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) with finite-width beam search. This work examines how this output interface constrains whether held-out targets enter finite returned lists, while distinguishing catalog-wide scoreability from empirical top-K support. We introduce two continuous-query paradigms: CQG-Single generates one retrieval query in a single pass, and CQG-AR autoregressively generates continuous residual updates, retaining step-wise decoding while removing the SID item-token vocabulary, code lookup, and discrete beam expansion. These designs thereby eliminate the SID-specific reachability constraint induced by finite-beam decoding and avoid the technical challenge of aligning a discrete SID vocabulary with the pretrained backbone's vector space. Both methods make every encoded item directly scoreable through dense or approximate-nearest-neighbor retrieval. title: NONSENSE: Non-Semantic Strings Expose Semanticity Gaps in Dense Retrieval
summary: Dense retrieval is central to modern search, question answering, and retrieval-augmented generation, where high similarity is often treated as evidence of semantic relevance. We examine how far this assumption can be stressed. NONSENSE is a black-box sparse-edit probe that constructs visibly non-semantic strings while forbidding query-term copying, optimizing only the dense similarity between a query and the string. Across five BEIR-style datasets and three popular single-vector retrievers, these strings frequently outscore the retriever's own best judged query-relevant passage (QRP), and often rank first in the full corpus. The result indicates a semanticity gap in the evaluated dense retrievers: nearest-neighbor status can be separated from passage-like meaning. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating dense retrievers not only by whether they retrieve relevant documents, but also by how reliably their similarity scores reflect semantic evidence.

The findings expose vulnerabilities in assuming high dense similarity always indicates semantic relevance.

title: ClusterRec: Cluster-Aware Recommendation with Large Language Models for Efficient and Scalable Inference
summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have significantly improved recommender systems by enabling richer semantic modeling of user preferences. However, existing LLM-based recommenders typically require expensive per-user inference over long interaction sequences, causing computational costs to scale rapidly with both model size and the number of users. To address this challenge, we propose ClusterRec, a framework that decouples LLM-based recommendation into two stages: (1) group-level preference modeling and (2) user-level personalization. Specifically, users are first clustered based on behavioral representations, and LLMs are employed to construct a group-level semantic representation for each cluster. Individual user representations are then constructed by integrating shared group representations with personalized collaborative filtering embeddings. This design amortizes LLM inference at the group level, substantially reducing computational overhead while preserving personalization. title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
summary: Efficient sequential recommendation has emerged as a promising paradigm for providing real-time personalized service. To deploy models under resource-constrained environment, model compression becomes a necessity, yet existing methods typically apply uniform compression ratios, overlooking the heterogeneity in user intent complexity. To address this, we propose RACE (Ranking-uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation), a framework that dynamically adapts both model structures and input sequences with uncertainty-aware compression ratios. To ensure capacity-adaptive inference, RACE captures the model's intrinsic uncertainty of its predictions and transforms it into a proactive resource allocator. title: SOARS: System One Assisted Reranking for Agentic Search
summary: Deep search agents address complex information needs through iterative retrieval and reasoning, where the relevance of retrieved evidence influences downstream performance. Existing rerankers improve retrieval effectiveness but introduce substantial latency and cost when invoked throughout the search trajectory. We introduce SOARS, a training-free framework leveraging a System One model for fast, calibrated relevance estimation. At each search step, SOARS selects query-relevant passages from long documents and reranks candidates in a single call, jointly considering the original question and agent-generated sub-query. Across six LLM backbones on BrowseComp-Plus and WebShaper, SOARS consistently improves answer accuracy and evidence recall while reducing search calls, end-to-end latency, and inference cost. On BrowseComp-Plus, it improves GPT-5.4 Mini's accuracy from 73.9% to 84.7% while reducing search calls from 23 to 14, demonstrating the potential of System One reranking for more effective and efficient deep search.

title: WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search
summary: We present WeSearch, a unified, model-centric retrieval framework for large-scale, continuously evolving content search. Prevailing methods assign documents fixed hierarchical Semantic IDs, implicitly assuming each document follows a single coherent semantic path-an assumption that often breaks down for multi-topic documents. Combined with relevance-aware training, compact document representations, and incremental index updates, this design enables weekly-or daily when needed-model refreshes. Deployed as the primary semantic retrieval path in WeChat Search alongside a lexical syntax tree, WeSearch shows consistent one-week A/B gains on corpora from hundreds of millions to billions of documents, and a one-month full-traffic A/B test confirms stable improvements of +0.68% CTR and +2.27% per-user article clicks, together with a 41% reduction in retrieval resource cost and a 19 ms reduction in graphic-text retrieval latency. title: ProgramGym: Scaling Training Environments for Long-Horizon Program Reproduction Agents
summary: Coding agents are increasingly used to build programs from scratch as software engineers do rather than to resolve issues within a repository or to generate a repository from a given requirements document. However, scalable verifiable training environments that force agents to discover what is required and to decide how the system should be designed remain scarce. Moreover, existing agent workflows also cannot sustain long-horizon development in which the agent explores the reference program before implementation. To address these challenges, we introduce ProgramGym, a framework consisting of Program-Env and Program-Agent for scalable training environments of long-horizon program reproduction agents. Specifically, Program-Env constructs verifiable training environments from repositories through a feedback-driven loop that repairs runtime sandbox builds and the quality of black-box tests. Using this novel pipeline, we obtain 1,648 training environments spanning C, C++, Go, and Rust. title: Graph-Informed Forecasting and Coordinated Replenishment: A Cost-Sensitive Study of Multi-Store Retail Inventory
summary: Retail networks with correlated demand shocks raise two separate questions: whether shared information improves forecasts, and whether better forecasts reduce inventory costs under shared capacity. Building on the integrated forecasting–replenishment perspective of MARIOD, we address both questions with a transparent 12-store, 300-day network featuring cluster structure, a two-day lead time, lost sales and an aggregate daily replenishment budget. Local ridge forecasts are compared with graph-lag forecasts that add lagged neighbor and cluster demand summaries, under independent equal-share ordering, proportional budget pooling and a standardized-deficit risk allocator. Across 20 seeds and four scenarios, graph features reduce forecast error in correlated settings, and proportional pooling lowers default-scenario cost by 7.37 units/day relative to equal-share ordering, establishing a strong low-complexity coordination baseline. title: Retrieval, Scoring, and Decoding Shape Performance and Stability in LLM-based Conversational Recommendation
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as rerankers in conversational recommender systems, yet measured gains depend strongly on the retrieval and inference protocol. With a shared semantic top-250 candidate pool and strict candidate-aware scoring, the best proprietary reranker reaches NDCG@10 of 0.1497, compared with 0.0939 for the strongest non-LLM baseline. The same reranker reaches 0.2925 in zero-shot generation, showing that unconstrained scoring can yield a much larger apparent advantage than matched-pool evaluation. No evaluated open-weight LLM outperforms the tuned shallow autoencoder baseline under this protocol. title: A hybrid emotion-aware recommendation framework integrating sentiment analysis, GRU-based sequence learning, and target-user modeling

A fuzzy inference module combines contextual, similarity, and target-user information to support interpretable decision-making under uncertain preferences, while a GRU network models temporal dependencies in user-item interaction sequences. The resulting representations are fused to generate personalized Top-N recommendations. Experiments conducted on large-scale Amazon e-commerce datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 0.43, precision of 0.61, recall of 0.59, F1-score of 0.60, Top-N accuracy of 0.51, and MRR of 0.53. title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Domain‐Agnostic Aspect‐Aware Recommendation
summary: The growth of e‐commerce and the corresponding increase in the number of online reviews have driven the demand for recommender systems that capture user preferences.
