tldr: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets.

title: Agent-Guided Configuration Tuning for SMT Solvers
summary: SMT solvers expose many configuration choices that determine how well their existing algorithms perform on a workload. We present, to our knowledge, the first workflow that uses general-purpose LLM agents to tune SMT solver configurations. Agents read solver documentation, source code, and persistent experiment records to propose option changes, and a deterministic harness measures each proposal, validates the returned models, and selects changes separately for each competition Division. Over roughly nine weeks, our tuning campaign recorded 4,545 proposals for cvc5 across 13 Divisions and 36 logics. We evaluate the tuned configurations on the 2026 and 2025 SMT-COMP ModelValidation benchmarks under a 24-second cutoff. On problems not used for training, they validate more problems than official cvc5 in ten of the 13 Divisions in 2026 and in eight in 2025, with geometric-mean gains of 7.8% and 6.8% across Divisions. On the complete official selections, which include training problems, the tuned floating-point counts exceed those of every individual competition participant in both years. tldr: SMT solvers expose many configuration choices that determine how well their existing algorithms perform on a workload. We present, to our knowledge, the first workflow that uses general-purpose LLM agents to tune SMT solver configurations.

title: Diagnosing Modality Reliability in Sparse E-Commerce Recommendation: A White-Box Routing Study
summary: Multimodal recommenders usually assume that fusing collaborative, visual, and textual signals improves accuracy. We treat this as a diagnostic question rather than an accuracy contest. Under interaction-level leave-one-out evaluation on three sparse Amazon categories, three findings emerge. First, text is the only modality that transfers; removing it lowers AUC by 0.23–0.25, while removing the visual stream changes AUC by at most 0.01 and removing collaborative ID features leaves it unchanged. Second, the apparent value of collaborative features is protocol-dependent. Full models reach AUC 0.97–0.99 under random splitting but only 0.71–0.74 under leave-one-out. The gap vanishes under a user-disjoint split, which is consistent with identity-side shortcuts rather than transferable signal. Third, white-box routing agrees with modality ablations at the dataset level, but is not seed-stable enough to serve as a per-instance explanation. title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
summary: This paper describes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server through which a general-purpose AI agent operates a discrete element engine, commercial or open-source, while the simulation runs. The agent submits a long simulation to the engine and, while it computes, reads the running model, changes it, or stops it. The human modeler stays at the engine's console and graphical interface throughout, and the agent sees what the modeler does there. The tools are derived from what the agent needs to do at the engine and are held to four principles: correctness, coverage, orthogonality and simplicity. Two documentation tools let the agent search the engine's manual and browse it level by level. Five execution tools let the agent run code in the engine, submit long simulations in the background, check on them, read the running model, and stop them. A bridge inside the engine serves these tools in a commercial DEM engine, PFC, and an open-source one, YADE. In a case study, a general-purpose agent calibrated a drained triaxial model of dense Toyoura sand against laboratory data in both engines, while the modeler worked at the same engine; the agent noticed the modeler's actions at the console…

title: Understanding Failure Patterns in LLM-Based Mathematical Optimization Modeling
summary: Industrial optimization involves complex constraints, making optimization modeling difficult to automate. Large language models (LLMs) have been explored for generating optimization models from natural language, but their reliability in end-to-end settings remains limited, often producing non-executable, infeasible, or feasible but incorrect solutions. In this work, we study failure modes in LLM-based optimization modeling by decomposing the process into three components: mathematical reasoning, solver usage, and domain knowledge, and constructing datasets that target each aspect. Using these datasets, we analyze how different components relate to errors and find that they are associated with different types of failure, although these relationships are not always strong or consistent. Furthermore, while combining these components improves execution reliability, feasible but incorrect solutions remain the dominant failure mode, suggesting a remaining gap between executability and correctness. These findings highlight limitations of current dataset designs and suggest the importance of data that better capture constraint completeness and formulation accuracy to enhance reliability.
tldr: Industrial optimization involves complex constraints, making optimization modeling difficult to automate. Large language models (LLMs) have been explored for generating optimization models from natural language, but their reliability in end-to-end settings remains limited, often producing non-executable, infeasible, or feasible but incorrect solutions.

title: When Direction Matters: Diagnosing Relational Instruction Following in Dense Retrieval
summary: Dense retrievers increasingly claim the ability to condition retrieval on natural-language relevance criteria beyond a short query. title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
summary: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. title: ELBO TDS: Temporal Distribution Shift Generalization for Industry-Scale Recommender Systems
summary: Temporal distribution shift (TDS) degrades the generalization of recommender systems: models trained on past interactions face systematically different user behavior in future time windows. While incremental training on recent data is widely used in industry production, it can over-adapt to transient patterns and exacerbate instability. Existing approaches such as invariant learning and self-supervised learning offer partial solutions but often suffer from unstable temporal generalization, representation collapse, or inefficient data utilization. To address these limitations, we propose ELBOTDS, a probabilistic framework for temporally robust recommendation. First, we identify key shifting factors on real-world production data and design a simple yet effective data augmentation strategy that simulate realistic time-varying factors to extend the training support. title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Long-horizon tasks require LLM agents to continually draw on information from earlier interactions. However, retaining the full history increases context costs, while compressing it risks losing details needed later, and the relevance of historical information often becomes apparent as the task progresses. To address these challenges, we propose FlowState, which treats execution state as memory that can be retained and revisited across requests, unifying current decision-making with the reuse of historical information. FlowState preserves semantically typed state nodes, their relations, and references to raw tool observations, separating persistent retention from on-demand access. Within a single execution loop, Incremental State Update (ISU) maintains the current state based on new inputs and feedback, while Progressive State Access (PSA) progressively reveals historical states and supporting evidence as needed during reasoning. Together, these mechanisms enable agents to reassess prior decisions in light of new information and guide subsequent actions. title: Aligning AI Teams
summary: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or coordinate in a group chat, do not reliably bring agent teams back to single-agent alignment behavior; (3) diffusion of responsibility substantially accounts for the safety gap: agents in teams are less likely to proactively check for system-level safety failures and more likely to ignore, rationalize, or deflect responsibility for issues when they arise; (4) having a designated safety lead agent ensure system-level safety, and having a coordinator agent publish a safety specifications document are …

title: Self-Evolving Memory for Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommendation has emerged as a promising end-to-end paradigm for personalized recommendation. In real-world recommendation scenarios, however, user preferences continuously evolve over time, making self-evolving an essential capability for generative recommender systems. Existing evolving strategies, such as continual retraining and distillation-based adaptation, directly update the shared model parameters using streaming interactions. Nevertheless, we find that directly applying such strategies to generative recommendation introduces a critical issue, termed evolution conflict . Specifically, heterogeneous preference shifts from different users are optimized within a fully shared autoregressive parameter space, causing dominant behavioral patterns to progressively dominate the model evolution process while underrepresented patterns become increasingly overlooked. To address this issue, we propose a self-evolving memory paradigm for generative recommendation, aiming to enable effective evolution across heterogeneous behavioral patterns. title: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
summary: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for later outputs. A blockwise protocol enforces this distinction through attention masks in full-attention layers and recurrent-state retention rules in linear-attention layers. The selected training sources contain 159.7M generation samples, 213.4M understanding samples, and 624.8K interleaved sequences. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation.

title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
summary: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains. Agents must pass each level to unlock the next, with later levels building on experience accumulated during earlier assignments. An evaluation agent assesses each submission against human-authored rubrics. We compare a single-submission setting with one that provides diagnostic feedback after failure and allows one revision. Across 17 harness-model configurations using frontier LLMs, feedback and revision yield a median completion gain of 5.3 percentage points. Yet the best-performing system clears…
tldr: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience.

title: EdgeWise: Bringing Long-Horizon Agents to the Edge via Selective Cloud Delegation
summary: Complex and long-horizon agent tasks often rely on frontier models deployed in the cloud to achieve strong performance. However, using these models for every step of a long-horizon trajectory incurs substantial inference cost, even though not all steps may require the same level of model capability. In this paper, we find that allocating the LLM to only a small subset of key steps can achieve performance comparable to full LLM execution while significantly reducing inference cost. Motivated by this observation, we propose EdgeWise, an edge-cloud collaboration framework that deploys an SLM on the local device as the primary solver and selectively delegates critical steps to a cloud LLM when stronger model capacity is needed. To enable autonomous delegation without additional models at inference time, we introduce a step-level RL method that jointly optimizes task solving and delegation, with fine-grained credit assignment for individual delegation decisions. We also introduce an external judge-based delegation strategy and use it to systematically investigate key design choices in edge-cloud collaboration, including when to delegate, how delegation decisions should be made, what co…
tldr: Complex and long-horizon agent tasks often rely on frontier models deployed in the cloud to achieve strong performance. However, using these models for every step of a long-horizon trajectory incurs substantial inference cost, even though not all steps may require the same level of model capability.

title: Analysis of Logistics Problems in National E-Commerce Companies: Causative Factors, Improvement Strategies, and Solution Recommendations
summary: Background. The rapid growth of Indonesia's e-commerce industry poses significant logistics challenges. This study examines logistics problems in a national e-commerce company that experienced a 20 an increase in delivery delays, a 15% increase in logistics costs, and an escalation of customer complaints. Objectives. This study aims to identify the factors causing the problem, analyze logistics strategies that need improvement, and formulate short- and long-term recommendations. Methods. This study uses a case study approach with qualitative descriptive analysis. Data were collected through literature review, operational report analysis, and observation of business processes. Results. The results showed that logistics problems stemmed from internal factors (warehouse capacity, WMS systems, dependence on courier partners) and external factors (seasonal demand volatility and fuel cost fluctuations). Conclusion. The improvement strategy focuses on optimizing inventory management, diversifying logistics partnerships, optimizing routes, and improving tracking transparency. Short-term recommendations include courier contract audits, establishing logistics command centers, and customer c…
tldr: Background. The rapid growth of Indonesia's e-commerce industry poses significant logistics challenges. This study examines logistics problems in a national e-commerce company that experienced a 20 an increase in delivery delays, a 15% increase in logistics costs, and an escalation of customer complaints. Objectives.

title: Research and Analysis on XGBoost, Random Forest, and Their Hybrid Models in Retail Sales Forecasting
summary: Retail sales forecasting plays a crucial role in inventory management, marketing planning, and supply-chain optimization, and the choice of model directly influences how well retailers respond to demand volatility, promotions, and seasonal patterns.With the growing complexity of retail sales forecasting, the use of machine learning models for data analysis has become increasingly important.This study reviews relevant literature to summarize the performance of XGBoost and Random Forest in retail sales forecasting, and analyzes the effectiveness of hybrid models combining these two algorithms.XGBoost features high prediction accuracy, effective regularization to mitigate overfitting, and strong capability in modeling nonlinear relationships and imbalanced data.Random Forest demonstrates high stability, robustness to noise, and excellence in feature importance analysis.Hybrid models combining XGBoost and Random Forest achieve more accurate and reliable forecasting results than single models.This study provides practical guidance for model selection in retail sales forecasting.In future work, more competitive hybrid models will be further explored and evaluated.

title: Recommender Systems: Privacy and Security
Bias in book recommendation: A survey
summary: Automated book recommendation is a compelling application given the rich and long-standing human tradition of writing and reading. The documented discrimination in the publishing world raises questions on the types of bias that can arise when algorithms are trained on user-book interactions. Various papers have studied recommender systems bias based on datasets from platforms where users share their opinions on books. In this paper, we conduct the first survey of computer science research on bias in book recommender systems. We survey 40 papers from top conferences and journals using the structured PRISMA methodology and provide an overview of the field. We map the existing literature into bias types, subjects and actions, and present key metrics and bias mitigation methods. We find that there is limited targeted research, fragmented evaluation practices, and a lack of engagement with the unique characteristics of the literary domain. Finally, we propose avenues for future work and make concrete suggestions for interdisciplinary research.

DHLab, KNAW Humanities Cluster, Amsterdam, Netherlands
tldr: Automated book recommendation is a compelling application given the rich and long-standing human tradition of writing and reading. The documented discrimination in the publishing world raises questions on the types of bias that can arise when algorithms are trained on user-book interactions. Various papers have studied recommender systems bias based on datasets from platforms where users share their opinions on books.

title: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator
summary: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks. We introduce SOLVE, a training-free, versatile and efficient agent policy: a multimodal LLM agent writes a sparse, ordered sequence of 6-DoF end-effector keyposes per call, observes the result, and writes the next, while a motion planner interpolates between them. The agent decides the number and spacing of keyposes for both fast long-range motion and fine-grained manipulation. This granularity matches the sparsity of teleoperated manipulation: most demonstrations in DROID can be compressed into a few keyposes instead of dense actions. SOLVE grounds keyposes with sparse depth queries answered by noisy sources, such as multi-view triangulation, stereo, or monocular depth, and copes with that noise itself. It also improves from execution feedback, reflecting on its own rollouts and distilling a few rules per task. SOLVE reaches state-of-the-art performance of 74.5% on RoboDojo and 84.5% on RoboLab, with only $1.7 per episode on average, 12x less than previous dense-control agent policies. On a real robot, the same agent achieves …
tldr: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks. We introduce SOLVE, a training-free, versatile and efficient agent policy: a multimodal LLM agent writes a sparse, ordered sequence of 6-DoF end-effector keyposes per call, observes the result, and writes the next, while a motion planner interpolates between them.

title: Learning the Platform, Not the Learner: Sequencing Shortcuts in the Offline Evaluation of Educational Recommender Systems and LLM Rankers
summary: Educational recommenders are usually compared offline, by how well they predict the next activity in logs of tutoring systems, learning applications and MOOCs, where the next activity is largely decided by the platform: teachers assign problem sets, tutors draw problems until mastery, engines select questions. On eight public datasets from five platforms, we compare four structural predictors, which use nothing about the learner beyond the last activity, with ten personalised recommenders and with open-weight LLM rankers from 0.5 to 7 billion parameters, under two protocols. The structural predictors reach between 0.81 and 1.00 of the best accuracy of any method (median 0.95), mostly through population transitions rather than the course order; the best personalised recommender is significantly better on five datasets, by 0.007 to 0.102 NDCG@10, and on Eedi in three of four training runs. Every method is far less accurate on steps along transitions never seen in training and on steps chosen by learners. LLM rankers look competent with random negatives but are never much better than a word-matching baseline, and with negatives that are plausible under the course structure they stay …
tldr: Educational recommenders are usually compared offline, by how well they predict the next activity in logs of tutoring systems, learning applications and MOOCs, where the next activity is largely decided by the platform: teachers assign problem sets, tutors draw problems until mastery, engines select questions.

title: Conformal Fair Decoding for Large Language Model Recommenders
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate personalized recommendations without task-specific training, but changing a protected attribute while holding interaction history fixed can alter the semantic content of recommended items. We study fairness control when model weights and full-vocabulary logits are unavailable. We propose Fair- Rec, an item-level decoding framework that uses an offline-calibrated semantic-disparity threshold and controls candidate selection as recommendation lists are generated. A hard variant filters candidates against the threshold; a soft variant trades off candidate likelihood and disparity while adapting a penalty using observed violations. Under an explicit uniform enforceability assumption, we establish a pathwise O(1/T) upper bound on the excess empirical violation rate of the soft decoder. Experiments on MovieLens-1M and Amazon Movies & TV using Qwen3-8B and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct show that the soft variant lowers measured counterfactual disparity relative to zero- =shot recommendation, UP5, and FACTER, while retaining competitive HR@10 and NDCG@10.
tldr: Large language models (LLMs) can generate personalized recommendations without task-specific training, but changing a protected attribute while holding interaction history fixed can alter the semantic content of recommended items. We study fairness control when model weights and full-vocabulary logits are unavailable.

title: R-BED: A Consequence-Aware Framework for System-Level AI Evaluation and Continuous Assurance
summary: Evaluations of AI systems usually report properties of a model, while decisions to deploy concern a configured system: a model together with prompts, tools, permissions, data, safeguards and an operating context. We ask how evidence about technical failures, deployment-control effectiveness and real-world consequences can be connected to defensible authorization decisions throughout the lifecycle of a deployed system. We present R-BED (Risk-Based Evaluability Design), a specification-level methodology with a fixed 6+4+3 architecture of thirteen diagnostic dimensions (technical failure, deployment controls, consequence and impact); a failure-mediated expected-loss identity that is kept separate from intended-behavior and misuse pathways; bounded evidence statuses with independence levels; a control assurance ladder; five authorization dispositions governed by eight rules; and a Continuous System Evaluation (CSE) layer in which evidence carries a configuration pin, an expiry and declared dependencies, so that a change invalidates evidence in proportion rather than wholesale. We work through a synthetic refund-agent walkthrough, with a deterministic script that reproduces every numbe…
tldr: Evaluations of AI systems usually report properties of a model, while decisions to deploy concern a configured system: a model together with prompts, tools, permissions, data, safeguards and an operating context. We ask how evidence about technical failures, deployment-control effectiveness and real-world consequences can be connected to defensible authorization decisions throughout the lifecycle of a deployed system.

title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses. Agents must select currently applicable skills from an expanding skill pool and prepare candidates for subsequent steps. We propose Skill Adapter, which enables personalized modification and online routing of general-purpose skills. The system distills local adjustments from user requirements and execution feedback and stores them as Adapters linked to general-purpose skills. The routing agent selects general-purpose skills and applicable Adapters based on the current subtask, execution progress, and environmental feedback, incrementally maintaining a task-level online skill library that the main LLM reads on demand. The system preloads candidates for subsequent nodes and rechecks their applicability once actual inputs are determined. Reinforcement learning optimizes the two types of decisions using modification gains a…
tldr: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses.

title: The Value Semantics Layer: Enabling Machine-Understandable Databases for Agentic AI
summary: As data systems increasingly support autonomous LLM-powered agents alongside human analysts, they require richer semantic infrastructure bridging analytical concepts and analytical operations. Existing metadata systems expose schemas, catalogs, lineage, and governance information, but provide limited support for representing operational semantics. We propose the Value Semantics Layer (VSL), an architectural abstraction that externalizes value semantics as persistent, planner-visible infrastructure. VSL introduces Value Semantic Types (VSTs), reusable operational semantic assertions capturing distributional, relational, process, quantitative, and policy-grounded semantics. Unlike descriptive metadata, VSTs enable planners to validate analytical operations, select appropriate operators, and guide analytical workflows. We present the motivation, formalization, architecture, and prototype realizations of VSL, and outline a research agenda toward AI-native semantic infrastructure for analytical systems.

tldr: As data systems increasingly support autonomous LLM-powered agents alongside human analysts, they require richer semantic infrastructure bridging analytical concepts and analytical operations. Existing metadata systems expose schemas, catalogs, lineage, and governance information, but provide limited support for representing operational semantics.

title: FLAIR-XGT: Local visual patch feature aggregation with multi-graph fusion for image-based recommendation
summary: Existing multimodal recommender systems discard fine-grained spatial information before recommendation training even starts by representing each product image as a single global vector, either a pooled CNN output or a Vision Transformer’s CLS token. We propose FLAIR-XGT, an image-based recommendation framework that uses three parallel graph networks (LightGCN, VisualGCN, and TextGCN) to jointly train representative local DINOv2 ViT-B/14 patch tokens (each covering a pixel region) end-to-end under a combined BPR + InfoNCE objective. Our primary scoring component, GlobalVis, combines the local patch tokens using a projector that is optimized in tandem with the recommender. In comparison to all fixed pre-extracted global-feature baselines, this joint training of local patch aggregation with multi-graph collaborative fusion produces NDCG@20 on Amazon Fashion ( over MMGCN) and NDCG@20 on Sports & Outdoors ( over MMGCN). We also study XGT, a user-conditioned cross-attention module that focuses spatial attention on user-relevant patches. A Graph Transformer block with a CF residual connection fuses the attended output. One important empirical finding is that XGT cross-attention performs …

tldr: Existing multimodal recommender systems discard fine-grained spatial information before recommendation training even starts by representing each product image as a single global vector, either a pooled CNN output or a Vision Transformer’s CLS token.

title: Intrinsic Attention as Navigator: A Non-Generative Retrieval Method for Multi-Hop Queries
summary: For multi-hop queries in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), it is crucial to accurately obtain evidence pieces. In this study, we propose a training-free method for multi-hop query retrieval, named Intrinsic Navigating-based Non-Generative Retrieval (IN-Retriever). Instead of generating intermediate reasoning text, the method extracts the bridging clue from the internal attention of the embedding model based on the current context and retrieved candidate documents. During iterative clue extraction and document retrieval, IN-Retriever strips away revealed clues from the embedded query vector and then reranks candidate documents in a targeted manner, thereby steering retrieval toward hidden next-hop evidence. In the experiments, we confirm the feasibility and effectiveness of using intrinsic attention signals to guide external multi-hop retrieval. Experimental results show that our method precisely collects sufficient documents to support multi-hop queries and significantly outperforms sparse and dense retrieval methods.
tldr: For multi-hop queries in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), it is crucial to accurately obtain evidence pieces. In this study, we propose a training-free method for multi-hop query retrieval, named Intrinsic Navigating-based Non-Generative Retrieval (IN-Retriever).

title: Learning from How Users Interpret: Personalizing Recommendation Explanation Order
summary: Personalized explanations typically adapt their content or presentation based on preferences, interaction histories, or other user characteristics. We examine whether regularities inferred from prior textual interpretations can support personalization of explanation organization. In a controlled within participant study with 122 participants, prior interpretations were represented along three dimensions: information selection, relative salience, and relational organization. The relational dimension was partially operationalized through co mobilization. These representations were aggregated into fixed historical profiles and used to organize otherwise identical explanation sentences. Participants encountered four organization procedures: the OWN historical profile, the DONOR historical profile, a population profile called POP, and a language model procedure using the historical profile called PROFILE LLM. Post exposure objective comprehension was the primary outcome. OWN achieved 86.5 percent correct responses, compared with 66.0 percent for DONOR, 63.9 percent for POP, and 73.0 percent for PROFILE LLM. Mixed effects analyses showed higher comprehension with OWN than with each alte…
affiliations: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Paris-Dauphine University , PSL Research University UMR CNRS 7243 , LAMSADE Paris , France
tldr: Personalized explanations typically adapt their content or presentation based on preferences, interaction histories, or other user characteristics. We examine whether regularities inferred from prior textual interpretations can support personalization of explanation organization.

title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
summary: AI agent harnesses play the critical role of providing LLMs with an interface to a computing environment. Recent studies show that AI agents' task-execution accuracy depends mostly on the LLM used, while harness-side variances such as system prompts or tools have minimal impact. Rather, such harness-side variances show a larger impact on the cost of agent executions, achieving cost reductions up to 2.6 times on the same model and task. To further explore these harness-side cost optimization opportunities, we analyze the cost accumulation patterns across various agent traces and identify system opportunities to reduce token use and LLM calls without modifying the model or affecting task accuracy. Based on this analysis, we design Agency, a harness interposition platform that provides a unified abstraction and allows easy and portable implementation of harness-side system optimizations on existing off-the-shelf harnesses such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Using Agency, we implement proof-of-concept optimization techniques based on our analysis and achieve cost reductions up to 35% across various real-world benchmarks on existing harnesses without compromising accuracy.
tldr: AI agent harnesses play the critical role of providing LLMs with an interface to a computing environment. Recent studies show that AI agents' task-execution accuracy depends mostly on the LLM used, while harness-side variances such as system prompts or tools have minimal impact. Rather, such harness-side variances show a larger impact on the cost of agent executions, achieving cost reductions up to 2.6 times on the same model and task.

title: LARF: Learning-aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance
summary: Query-document relevance estimation is a core component of AI-native search systems, where a model must assess whether retrieved documents satisfy users' information needs under complex, multi-dimensional criteria. However, directly applying large language models (LLMs) to this task remains challenging because conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides limited supervision for domain-specific judgment rationales, while standard trajectory-level reinforcement learning (RL) objectives do not explicitly enforce margin separation among adjacent ordinal relevance labels. Moreover, although such reasoning can be useful during training, chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning is impractical for latency-sensitive online ranking. These challenges make it difficult to resolve ambiguous decision boundaries. We propose a three-stage framework LARF (Learning-Aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance): it first performs cold-start SFT on strategically selected samples with multi-agent guided CoT rationales, then applies discriminative GRPO with attribute-wise, list-wise, and rule-consistency rewards together with a margin loss on the terminal relevance token, and finally distills the tea…
tldr: Query-document relevance estimation is a core component of AI-native search systems, where a model must assess whether retrieved documents satisfy users' information needs under complex, multi-dimensional criteria.

title: Calibrated Early Termination with Bounded Optimality Gaps for Constrained Vector Search
summary: Vector search over learned embeddings is the retrieval layer of recommendation and retrieval-augmented generation, and many applications cap how many answer items one category may contribute. Graph indexes answer a query by best-first traversal, and where it stops determines its cost and whether its answer is exact. We study early termination for such constrained $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) queries, with plain $k$-NN as a special case, and seek the cheapest stopping rule whose answer is exact with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$. Learned early-termination methods instead target average recall, which does not guarantee exact answers. Multiple testing can calibrate any parameterized stopping rule to our target, but it cannot tell how much a better rule with the same risk and observations would save. Answering this needs a lower bound on the optimum of a rule family too large to enumerate, valid for the query population. Our key idea is to declare the observations a rule may use and to consider every rule monotone in them. Risk-constrained stopping then becomes a linear program over an order polytope, whose Lagrangian minimizers form a nested chain of staircase rules computed …

tldr: Vector search over learned embeddings is the retrieval layer of recommendation and retrieval-augmented generation, and many applications cap how many answer items one category may contribute. Graph indexes answer a query by best-first traversal, and where it stops determines its cost and whether its answer is exact.

title: XBridge: Entity-Grounded Latent Bridge for Heterogeneous LLM Communication
summary: Heterogeneous multi-agent LLM systems, where agents are powered by different model families, can outperform homogeneous configurations by reducing redundant reasoning patterns. Yet existing communication protocols either operate through text, discarding the sender's internal representations, or require architectural homogeneity for latent-level transfer. We identify the entity grounding problem in cross-architecture communication: cross-attention bridges that transfer continuous representations across different LLM families suffer from rare-token compression collapse, where entity identity is lost in the continuous bottleneck (bridge-only F1 ~30%). We propose XBRIDGE, a decode-free communication protocol that addresses this through two mechanisms. Lexical Anchor Mapping (LAM) maps the sender's original context tokens to the receiver's vocabulary, providing discrete entity anchors. A Latent Enrichment Bridge (LEB) lets the receiver query the sender's hidden states for contextual enrichment. The entity anchors ground the bridge's contextual signals to specific entities through the receiver's own self-attention. Across three model families (Llama, Qwen, and Mistral), seven benchmarks…
tldr: Heterogeneous multi-agent LLM systems, where agents are powered by different model families, can outperform homogeneous configurations by reducing redundant reasoning patterns. Yet existing communication protocols either operate through text, discarding the sender's internal representations, or require architectural homogeneity for latent-level transfer.

title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
summary: Developers download quantized large language models (LLMs) from public registries to run them locally. None of the registries we examined documented functional testing of their files. We tested all 305 eligible code-capable GGUF tags (the llama.cpp format) across 15 model lines in the official Ollama library, plus 22 popular Hugging Face community files. A 15-task code screen identified suspects, which we retested on all 164 HumanEval+ tasks. Seven official tags (2.3%) solved at most six of them. All were low-bit quantizations of models with at most four billion parameters. We rebuilt five suspect files from the original weights. All five registry files matched our uncalibrated rebuilds tensor for tensor, so none was corrupted. Exact reproducibility did not imply function. With the weights, toolchain and tensor mix held fixed, adding an importance matrix raised Qwen2.5-Coder-3B scores at three quantization levels from zero to 76-113 of 164 tasks. The same uncalibrated recipe left the smaller Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B functional, showing that the recipe alone does not predict failure. None of 66 sampled tags that passed the screen was non-functional. We release the audit data and the quan…
tldr: Developers download quantized large language models (LLMs) from public registries to run them locally. None of the registries we examined documented functional testing of their files. We tested all 305 eligible code-capable GGUF tags (the llama.cpp format) across 15 model lines in the official Ollama library, plus 22 popular Hugging Face community files. A 15-task code screen identified suspects, which we retested on all 164 HumanEval+ tasks.

title: Who Remembers What? Multi-Granularity Memory Extraction for Multi-User, Multi-Agent Interaction
summary: Self-evolving agents improve their own skills, memory, and harness code from experience without retraining the base LLM, and group-evolving agents go further by sharing these lessons across agents. Yet most such systems overlook that sharing across users and heterogeneous agents requires deciding who can benefit from each lesson and what information must remain private. We present MixUA, a memory system that distills independent user-agent trajectories into lessons and assigns each lesson to a user-agent pair, user, agent, or global scope according to whom it benefits and what it may disclose. For evaluation, we introduce CrossLearnBench, a mixed-user-agent benchmark that pairs established agent tasks with user preferences and privacy probes that test whether private facts leak into memory other users can read. With five users and seven agents, MixUA raises pass rates by up to 16 points over no memory and 5 over a single global memory, even on tasks previously tried only by other users on other agents. It retains up to 90% of previously stated preferences, and at most 0.02% of privacy probes find a planted private fact in a forbidden scope. We hope MixUA offers a scalable path tow…
tldr: Self-evolving agents improve their own skills, memory, and harness code from experience without retraining the base LLM, and group-evolving agents go further by sharing these lessons across agents. Yet most such systems overlook that sharing across users and heterogeneous agents requires deciding who can benefit from each lesson and what information must remain private.

title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories
summary: Standard coding-agent benchmarks primarily evaluate binary task success, treating execution as a black box and obscuring the behaviors that produce those outcomes. We analyze a large corpus of 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 agent configurations spanning 117 unique models. To enable comparisons across heterogeneous agent interfaces, we develop a rule-based parser that maps raw execution traces to high-level actions such as repository search, file editing, and test execution, and audit its predictions against a six-model consensus reference on 500 events. We find that agents with similar solve rates can nevertheless differ substantially in how they explore, modify and verify code. Moreover, without using task outcomes, token counts, or tool names as features, aggregate behavioral profiles retrieve the corresponding agent stack across disjoint repository sets and programming languages, although task composition is not fully controlled in the cross-repository setting. Through analyses of frontier models and agent scaffolds, we further show that scaffold choice and reasoning effort systematically shift agents' search, editing, and testing behavior. We release the deterministic…
tldr: Standard coding-agent benchmarks primarily evaluate binary task success, treating execution as a black box and obscuring the behaviors that produce those outcomes. We analyze a large corpus of 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 agent configurations spanning 117 unique models.

title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
summary: Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. We introduce Trajectory2Gym, which constructs executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and derives supervision only from grounded decisions in their realized executions. Structural-support selection allocates the resulting experience, while parent-normalized supervised fine-tuning preserves the semantic interaction as the unit of training weight. This reframes trajectory generation as the deliberate construction of learnable interaction experience, rather than the collection of successful trajectories. Across five Qwen3 scales, Trajectory2Gym improves Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL at every tested scale, increasing the equal-weight three-benchmark m…
tldr: Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time.

title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and τ-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of…
tldr: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges.

title: Correcting to Predict: Pseudo-Value Correction for Multimodal Attribute Value Extraction
summary: Product attribute value extraction (AVE) is a fundamental task in e-commerce, aiming to identify specific values of predefined attributes from multimodal product profiles such as text and images. While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown promise for AVE, they face challenges in extracting implicit attributes that require joint reasoning over visual and textual cues, often confusing semantically similar values. However, existing methods often fail to resolve such ambiguities because the correct value often depends on subtle multimodal cues that are easy to miss or override. To address this challenge, we propose Correcting to Predict (C2P), a framework that treats attribute extraction as a correction process. Given an initial pseudo-value such as a retrieved candidate or placeholder, the model learns to correct it using multimodal evidence. During training, diverse pseudo-values help the model learn evidence-based correction behavior, and a self-consistency refinement stage further reduces sensitivity to pseudo-value perturbations. At inference, a fixed placeholder triggers the learned correction behavior, enabling efficient single-pass prediction without online retr…
affiliations: Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group, Hangzhou, China
tldr: Product attribute value extraction (AVE) is a fundamental task in e-commerce, aiming to identify specific values of predefined attributes from multimodal product profiles such as text and images. While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown promise for AVE, they face challenges in extracting implicit attributes that require joint reasoning over visual and textual cues, often confusing semantically similar values.

title: Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents
summary: Recursive language-model agents decompose tasks and delegate subtasks to child instances of the same policy, forming a tree of work. Training them, however, is hard: the final outcome is verifiable, but the self-invented intermediate subtasks are numerous and carry no ground truth. Existing methods score each node with a verifier or judge, which is costly at scale and blind to decomposition quality. We argue that a recursive agent must learn three coupled capabilities within one set of weights: decomposing problems into subtasks, solving them, and evaluating the outcomes, each requiring its own training signal. SERA (Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents) turns evaluation into a learned capability of the policy itself. Before delegating, the parent writes a rubric of weighted success criteria for each child subtask; a ranking objective against verified outcomes then trains rubric generation so that the criteria track genuine subtask success. In addition, a complementary leaf-coverage signal provides direct credit for task decomposition. Our central finding is that training the policy to generate aligned rubrics is what drives the gains: because the same weights both evaluate and execut…
tldr: Recursive language-model agents decompose tasks and delegate subtasks to child instances of the same policy, forming a tree of work. Training them, however, is hard: the final outcome is verifiable, but the self-invented intermediate subtasks are numerous and carry no ground truth. Existing methods score each node with a verifier or judge, which is costly at scale and blind to decomposition quality.

title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
summary: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve…
tldr: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity.

title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Long-horizon agents accumulate progress in persistent task state, yet repeatedly process interaction histories describing how that progress was achieved. This raises a natural question: can long-horizon context instead be organized around reusable progress rather than the history that produced it? In this paper, we introduce CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime that organizes continuation around reusable task objects. Rather than treating compressed histories or reconstructed accounts of progress as the primary basis for continuation, CarryOn builds a context view from continuation carriers, complementary execution context, and a live tail of recent interactions. A core challenge is keeping this reusable basis valid after its surrounding history is retired: how can CarryOn update the basis without reconstructing the full representation at every fold? CarryOn maintains carrier records across folds, revising affected records against bound evidence and applicable environment checks while carrying forward unaffected records and jointly updating execution context. Experiments on OSWorld 2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus show improved gains of 5.8% and 7.0% while reducing total token usage…
tldr: Long-horizon agents accumulate progress in persistent task state, yet repeatedly process interaction histories describing how that progress was achieved. This raises a natural question: can long-horizon context instead be organized around reusable progress rather than the history that produced it? In this paper, we introduce CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime that organizes continuation around reusable task objects.

title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
summary: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to provide continuous personalized assistance by retaining user information across interactions. Existing systems support this process through fact extraction, organization, updating, and retrieval, but largely maintain memories as independent facts. This fact-centric paradigm may overlook how new facts update, constrain, or conflict with earlier ones, while leaving their applicability, role, and priority for the current request implicit. In this paper, we introduce EvoMemState, a state-centric framework that augments persistent facts with two complementary states: Relational States that capture how facts remain valid and relate to one another as memory evolves, and a Reasoning State that determines how these facts should be applied to the current request. Specifically, EvoMemState consists of three key components: (i) Ontology-Guided Memory State Induction extracts Persistent Facts and constructs Relational States that maintain their validity, scope, and evolving relations. (ii) RL-Based State Evolution internalizes memory-use experience into a policy through reinforcement learning to generate a request-specific Reasoning…
tldr: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to provide continuous personalized assistance by retaining user information across interactions. Existing systems support this process through fact extraction, organization, updating, and retrieval, but largely maintain memories as independent facts.

title: TestPrism: Rethinking Test Evaluation Beyond a Single Reference
summary: Large language model (LLM) coding agents have advanced test generation across diverse programming tasks. However, the common practice of evaluating tests against a single reference solution overlooks alternative valid implementations and can overstate test quality. We introduce TestPrism, comprising 300 test tasks from 17 sources and 3000 candidate implementations, evenly split between valid and invalid solutions. Its primary metric, Joint Success Function, requires the generated tests to fail on the initial program state, accept every valid candidate, and reject every invalid candidate. Across fourteen baseline coding agent configurations, Joint Success Function reaches only 28.00%, whereas single reference success reaches 59.67%. Our analysis reveals missed behaviors, unsupported assertions, and faulty test construction. To address these weaknesses, we introduce TestHelix, which combines heterogeneous synthesis of test and repair pairs with peer cross validation and recursive self improvement (RSI). Across two models, TestHelix improves Joint Success Function by 8.67 to 9.00 percentage points over the native harness comparators in the TestHelix evaluation
tldr: Large language model (LLM) coding agents have advanced test generation across diverse programming tasks. However, the common practice of evaluating tests against a single reference solution overlooks alternative valid implementations and can overstate test quality. We introduce TestPrism, comprising 300 test tasks from 17 sources and 3000 candidate implementations, evenly split between valid and invalid solutions.

title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
summary: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the current state, Anticipate action effects, Plan a feasible course, Act through an interface or body, and Verify the outcome. Defined by function rather than architecture, these capabilities let PAPAV identify what all three share and then compare MMEAs with MMAs and with RSs. Five physical constraints, from partial observability to unverifiable outcomes, leave fewer choices fixed in advance and less room to reverse errors. Across 64 benchmarks, explicit evaluation centers on Act; only 5 assess Anticipate and 3 assess Verify, leaving both largely hidden behind task success. These constraints als…
tldr: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback.

title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
summary: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathem…
tldr: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency.

title: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents
summary: Long-horizon coding agents need timely corrections, yet feedback can be ineffective or even harmful when it misjudges ongoing work or fails to address the underlying problem. Existing critics focus on evaluating trajectories and generating feedback, but rarely track what happens after feedback is delivered. We present Opera, a verbal critic framework that treats each correction as a persistent note, followed until the diagnosed problem is resolved. Opera decides when to review through periodic and event-driven triggers, diagnoses issues with typed operators, audits feedback against visible evidence before delivery, and tracks the agent's subsequent actions to distinguish mere compliance from actual resolution. As a test-time critic, Opera improves the resolve rate of non-critic agents by up to 12.4, 15.0, and 8.9 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a SWE-Bench Pro subset, and DeepSWE v1.1, respectively, across four policy models, and achieves the highest mean resolve rate among competitive critic baselines on all three benchmarks, and also improves policy models when the policy critiques itself. Beyond inference, Opera-guided rollouts provide approximately on-policy training …
tldr: Long-horizon coding agents need timely corrections, yet feedback can be ineffective or even harmful when it misjudges ongoing work or fails to address the underlying problem. Existing critics focus on evaluating trajectories and generating feedback, but rarely track what happens after feedback is delivered.

title: AgentBaton: Efficient Model Collaboration in Agentic Tasks
summary: Solving long-horizon agentic tasks requires language agents to interact with their environments over multiple steps, and reliable performance often comes from the expensive capable models available through cloud providers. Meanwhile, alternative efficient models with inferior performance but a much lower cost are emerging, including lower-tier cloud models and smaller open-weights models deployable on local hardware. This raises a natural question that remains less explored than traditional query-level routing: can capable and efficient models collaborate within a single long-horizon agentic task to substantially reduce cost while preserving task accuracy? In this paper, we systematically investigate key design choices for such collaboration through model handoffs, where one model takes over from another, focusing on handoff direction and context transfer. We find that efficient-to-capable handoffs generally underperform capable-only execution with limited or even no cost reduction, whereas capable-to-efficient handoffs at suitable stages of task progress largely preserve or even improve accuracy while substantially reducing cost. These findings suggest that a one-time, simple, we…
tldr: Solving long-horizon agentic tasks requires language agents to interact with their environments over multiple steps, and reliable performance often comes from the expensive capable models available through cloud providers. Meanwhile, alternative efficient models with inferior performance but a much lower cost are emerging, including lower-tier cloud models and smaller open-weights models deployable on local hardware.

title: You don't need long context
summary: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on long-horizon software engineering tasks even when taking at most one action per context, and based on that we outline the concept of semantic state space models (SSSMs). Our findings question the need for long-context language models.
tldr: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts.

title: THE EVOLUTION OF SOCIAL COMMERCE: A HISTORICAL ANALYSIS OF WEBSITE FEATURES AND DIGITAL INTERACTIONS
summary: Social commerce represents one of the most significant transformations in digital retail, merging social media's interactive capabilities with e-commerce transactional functionality. This research traces the evolutionary trajectory of social commerce from its nascent stages in the early 2000s through its current sophisticated implementations, examining how website features and digital interactions have transformed consumer purchasing behavior. Through systematic analysis of platform developments, feature innovations, and user engagement patterns across two decades, we document how social commerce evolved from simple product sharing mechanisms to comprehensive ecosystems integrating user-generated content, live streaming, influencer marketing, and artificial intelligence-driven personalization. Our historical analysis reveals distinct developmental phases: the foundational period (2005-2010) characterized by basic social sharing features, the integration era (2011-2015) marked by dedicated social commerce platforms and Facebook commerce initiatives, the mobile acceleration phase (2016-2019) dominated by Instagram shopping and messaging-based commerce, and the immersive experience p…
tldr: Social commerce represents one of the most significant transformations in digital retail, merging social media's interactive capabilities with e-commerce transactional functionality. This research traces the evolutionary trajectory of social commerce from its nascent stages in the early 2000s through its current sophisticated implementations, examining how website features and digital interactions have transformed consumer purchasing behavior.

title: A comparative study of linear regression and decision trees for predicting consumer purchase intention across consumption scenarios of different complexity
summary: With the development of e-commerce, social media marketing and digital operations, enterprises can obtain a large amount of consumer data such as prices, revenues, discounts, product ratings, browsing frequencies and historical purchase records. How to utilize these data to predict consumers' purchase intentions has become an important issue in business analysis and precise marketing. This paper compares the prediction characteristics of linear regression and decision trees in different complexity consumption scenarios. Through literature research, simulation data analysis and comparative analysis, two types of experiments are constructed: the first type only sets an approximately linear relationship between product prices and purchase intentions; the second type adds income, discounts, ratings, browsing frequencies and historical purchase frequencies, and sets threshold effects and variable interactions. The research results show that in simple linear scenarios, linear regression can achieve slightly better prediction performance with lower complexity; in multi-variable, non-linear and interactive relationship scenarios, the prediction error of decision trees is lower. The paper …
tldr: With the development of e-commerce, social media marketing and digital operations, enterprises can obtain a large amount of consumer data such as prices, revenues, discounts, product ratings, browsing frequencies and historical purchase records. How to utilize these data to predict consumers' purchase intentions has become an important issue in business analysis and precise marketing.

title: SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills
summary: An agent skill that succeeded yesterday may be executable today without being justified for reuse today. Tests may cover only observable contract clauses, outcome oracles may be absent, evaluations may inherit the same erroneous specification, and permissions or dependencies may change between validation and invocation. We argue that the appropriate unit of prospective trust is a Warranted Reuse Claim (WRC): a defeasible, claim-specific authorization tied to a versioned skill, target context, evidence, assumptions, and identified defeaters. The paper sharpens this position through Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport (WPET), a proposed discipline for deciding which historical evidence remains admissible after context change. It distinguishes evidence admissibility from truth of the supported safety or effectiveness claim; states a conditional preservation result and its limits; specifies three-valued applicability and asymmetric context-transfer judgments; and illustrates how provenance dependence and policy-invalidating changes alter authorization. We explicitly relate the proposal to assurance cases, contracts, and skill-library maintenance rather than claiming novelty for thei…
tldr: An agent skill that succeeded yesterday may be executable today without being justified for reuse today. Tests may cover only observable contract clauses, outcome oracles may be absent, evaluations may inherit the same erroneous specification, and permissions or dependencies may change between validation and invocation.

title: Interactive Proofs as a Unified Framework for Evaluating and Leveraging Verifiable Proof Generation by LLM Agents
summary: Recent advances in LLM-assisted theorem proving and program verification have attracted widespread attention. Beyond determining whether a proposition is true, LLM agents must produce evidence that can be independently checked by humans or formal verification tools. To evaluate the underlying, protocol-agnostic ability of LLM agents to construct verifiable proofs-rather than their proficiency with any particular proof language or verification tool, we introduce Merlin-Bench. Drawing on interactive proof systems from computational complexity theory, we cast an LLM agent as the prover: under a designated protocol, the agent interacts with a formal verifier to substantiate its claimed answer to a problem instance. We develop an automated framework for constructing test cases and use it to create 100 cases across 15 problem families, each formulated within this prover-verifier framework. Experiments with 10 frontier LLMs across multiple agent harnesses show that reliably producing verifiable proofs in accordance with specified protocols remains a substantial challenge. Our case studies further provide actionable insights into improving agents' ability to generate verifier-accepted pro…
tldr: Recent advances in LLM-assisted theorem proving and program verification have attracted widespread attention. Beyond determining whether a proposition is true, LLM agents must produce evidence that can be independently checked by humans or formal verification tools.

title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. However, these results only provide a partial explanation of why the agent hallucinates. The probe direction is sensitive to prompt formatting, losing much of its steering effect after a minor change to how actions are represented. Additionally, circuit identification can be difficult as the computation is distributed across multiple components and positions, and the information the agent relies on varie…
tldr: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures.

title: How Generative Models Generate: A Concise Guide to the Generative AI Landscape
summary: The rapidly expanding generative AI landscape brings together methods that differ in architecture, learning objective, mathematical representation and sampling procedure. A concise, selectively organised technical guide can provide an accessible starting point for developing a coherent understanding of this increasingly complex landscape. This article takes a generation-centred approach, connecting how models produce new observations with the modelling and learning principles that make generation possible. We develop a two-level perspective: first, distinguishing three recurring generation routes-direct transformation or decoding, sequential conditional construction, and iterative updating or transport; and second, examining the modelling and learning principles underlying these routes. Representative approaches are introduced through their key components, learning objectives and sampling procedures. We then examine their broader connections, including how different architectures and generation mechanisms can overlap or be combined. By bringing together essential technical explanations within a compact conceptual framework, the article aims to help readers develop a working unders…
affiliations: Department of Computer Science , University of Huddersfield , UK
tldr: The rapidly expanding generative AI landscape brings together methods that differ in architecture, learning objective, mathematical representation and sampling procedure. A concise, selectively organised technical guide can provide an accessible starting point for developing a coherent understanding of this increasingly complex landscape.

title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
summary: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient. To evaluate this capability of LLM agents in the hardware domain, we present ChiProgramBench, 18 tasks derived from open-source processors, accelerators, codecs, transforms, interconnects, and control circuits. Agents can only drive and read the pins of a hidden, stateful simulated reference, then submit a gate-level netlist made of public library cells. Agents work in two settings: black-box discovery gives only anonymized functional pins and the interfaces of fixed memories, while function-guided reconstruction adds the circuit's purpose and each pin's role. Hidden test cases compare outputs with the reference cycle by cycle; power, delay, and area earn credit relative to the reference only when every case passes. Across 432 trials of 6 LLM agent configurations, successful agents recover algorithms and numerical conventions, yet only 12.0% of black-box and 14.8% of function-guided trials pass every case. Function-guided r…
tldr: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient.

title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances
summary: Commercial solvers are the standard tool for difficult scheduling problems. We study whether a frontier large language model, used as a coding agent with open-source tools only, can match them in quality and speed. We report every run, and independent checkers verify every schedule. On the 100,000-operation job shop tai_100_1000_1, an agent-written solver reached 525,515, below OptalCP, Hexaly, and CP Optimizer. Unchanged, it improved all ten instances of the family and closed two. With equal budgets on the same workstation, it ended 0.0-1.8% above the lower bound, against 2.6-5.8% for CP Optimizer and 2.4-4.4% for Hexaly. On the Behnke-Geiger flexible job shops, an agent-written tabu search improved 11 of 32 open instances. With two transport robots, an agent-written solver improved seven of ten MKT instances. New lower bounds show that four published MKT values cannot be attained on the distributed instance files. Agent-run improvement campaigns closed eight further instances.
